### Photos and text over photos

- **Hero overlay.** A thin gradient over hero photos, from Navy black `#051925` on the text side to
  Ocean `#037AA6` on the subject side, at 15 to 30% opacity, so warm light still glows through. The
  text side is darker; the subject side stays clear.
- Put text over a photo only on a calm, high contrast area. The hero overlay is too thin to fix
  contrast on its own: white text over a bright area under it is about 2:1. Use the overlay only
  where the text side of the photo is already dark and calm, and check the text reaches 4.5:1 (3:1
  for large headlines). Otherwise move the text, or set it on a solid Navy, Black or Deep Teal
  block. `propellant-hero` always sets white text, so choose its photo with this in mind.
- The [images guide](/guidelines/images/#brand-photography) covers which photos to use.

## The Propellant stylesheet

Some guides use a small stylesheet that loads the exact fonts and adds a few ready made classes,
such as `propellant-headline` and `propellant-button`. It only styles elements you add a class to,
so it never changes the rest of your site. Load it with this line, wherever a guide tells you to:

```html
<link
  rel="stylesheet"
  href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/masschallenge/propellant-web@v2.0.0/dist/website.css"
/>
```

The `@v2.0.0` part pins your site to one release, so it never changes under you. A complete
example page is in [`examples/website.html`](https://github.com/masschallenge/propellant-web/blob/v2.0.0/examples/website.html).

**Type**

| Class | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `propellant-text` | Body font, line height and Black text for a whole page or section. |
| `propellant-headline` | Heading 1: the headline, in Oswald SemiBold capitals. |
| `propellant-headline-accent` | Wrap the payoff of a headline in it: Teal on light, Cyan on dark. |
| `propellant-eyebrow` | The tracked Oswald label above a headline. |
| `propellant-title-1` | Heading 2. |
| `propellant-title-2` or `propellant-subhead` | Heading 3, the subhead: card titles and section labels. |
| `propellant-title-3` | Heading 4. |
| `propellant-body` | Paragraph. |
| `propellant-caption` | Paragraph small, in Slate (White on dark), for dates and notes. |
| `propellant-stat` | The big stat, in Oswald Bold. Pair it with an eyebrow label. |
| `propellant-link` | An underlined link: Teal on light, Cyan on dark. |

**Buttons and accents**

| Class | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `propellant-button` | The primary pill button. Works on `<a>` and `<button>`. |
| `propellant-button propellant-button-secondary` | The secondary, outlined button. |
| `propellant-tag` | A rectangular Yellow event tag, such as EVENTS or NEWS. |
| `propellant-accent-rule` | A short Yellow rule, the one warm accent on a page. |

**Sections and blocks**

| Class | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `propellant-section-white`, `propellant-section-warm-white` | Light sections. |
| `propellant-section-angled` | A light section with the pale tint rising on an angle. |
| `propellant-section-navy`, `propellant-section-black`, `propellant-section-deep-teal` | Dark sections. Text turns White, links Cyan and buttons Cyan outlines. |
| `propellant-brand-band` | The same as `propellant-section-navy`. Kept so existing pages keep working. |
| `propellant-notch` | Add it to any section to draw the notch below it, in that section's color. |
| `propellant-card` | A white card with square corners and Teal titles, even inside a dark section. |
| `propellant-numbered`, `propellant-numbered-number` | A numbered block: heavy rule, Teal number. |
| `propellant-photo` | A photo with square corners that fits its column. |
| `propellant-hero` | A dark hero with the hero overlay. Put the photo inside it as an image with `propellant-hero-image`, or set it as the section's background image. |
| `propellant-hero-subject-left` | Add it to a hero whose subject is on the left, so the overlay darkens the right. |

A dark section with an eyebrow, a two toned headline, white cards and a notch:

```html
<section class="propellant-section-navy propellant-notch">
  <p class="propellant-eyebrow">Your eyebrow</p>
  <h2 class="propellant-headline">
    Your lead phrase <span class="propellant-headline-accent">your payoff</span>
  </h2>
  <div class="propellant-card">
    <h3 class="propellant-subhead">Card title</h3>
    <p class="propellant-body">Card text.</p>
  </div>
  <a class="propellant-button" href="/apply">Apply now</a>
</section>
```

## Keep it maintainable

- **Settings before code.** If something can be set in the builder's style settings, set it there.
- **Keep custom CSS short and labeled.** Paste only the snippets from these guides, and keep the
  comment line at the top of each so the next person knows where it came from.
- **Do not fight the theme.** If a theme setting and a snippet disagree, change the setting.
- **Check the published site and a phone.** Some code only runs on the published site, and every
  builder has a mobile view worth checking.

# Plain HTML

Source: https://propellant.masschallenge.org/web/websites/html/

If you write your own HTML pages, Propellant takes one line to set up. You will end up with our
fonts, colors, headlines, buttons and dark and light sections on any page, in about ten minutes.

## Before you start

- A text editor and the HTML files for your site.
- The [website spec](/web/websites/) open in another tab.
- Somewhere to host the pages. Any static host works.

## Part 1: Load the stylesheet

Add this line inside the `<head>` of every page, before your own stylesheets:

```html
<link
  rel="stylesheet"
  href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/masschallenge/propellant-web@v2.0.0/dist/website.css"
/>
```

That one file loads Lato (as Propellant Sans) and Oswald, defines every Propellant color and size,
and adds the class names below. It does not restyle anything you have not given a class to.

## Part 2: Use the classes

The [website spec](/web/websites/#the-propellant-stylesheet) lists every class. The ones you will
use most:

| Class | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `propellant-text` | Body font, line height and text color. Put it on `<body>` so the whole page uses it. |
| `propellant-eyebrow` | The tracked Oswald label above a headline. |
| `propellant-headline` | Heading 1: Oswald SemiBold, in capitals. Use it once or twice per page. |
| `propellant-headline-accent` | The payoff of a two toned headline: Teal on light, Cyan on dark. |
| `propellant-title-1`, `propellant-subhead`, `propellant-title-3` | Heading 2, Heading 3 and Heading 4, in Oswald capitals. |
| `propellant-body` | Paragraph text. |
| `propellant-caption` | Small print, such as dates and notes. |
| `propellant-link` | An underlined link: Teal on light, Cyan on dark. |
| `propellant-button` | The primary pill button. Works on `<a>` and `<button>`. |
| `propellant-button propellant-button-secondary` | The secondary, outlined button. |
| `propellant-section-navy`, `propellant-section-black`, `propellant-section-deep-teal` | Dark sections. Text turns White, links Cyan and buttons Cyan outlines. |
| `propellant-section-white`, `propellant-section-warm-white`, `propellant-section-angled` | Light sections. The angled one has the pale tint rising on an angle. |
| `propellant-notch` | The downward notch below a section, in that section's color. |
| `propellant-card` | A white card with square corners and Teal titles. |
| `propellant-numbered` | A numbered block. Put the number in `propellant-numbered-number`. |
| `propellant-hero` | A dark hero with the hero overlay over a photo. |

## Part 3: Build a page

Copy this into a new file named `index.html`, open it in a browser, and change the words:

```html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
    <title>Your page title</title>
    <link
      rel="stylesheet"
      href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/masschallenge/propellant-web@v2.0.0/dist/website.css"
    />
    <style>
      body { margin: 0; }
      section { padding: 96px 24px; }
      .content { max-width: 720px; margin: 0 auto; display: grid; gap: 16px; }
      .actions { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 12px; }
      .cards, .numbered { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(14rem, 1fr)); gap: 24px; }
      h1, h2, h3, p { margin: 0; }
      @media (max-width: 640px) { section { padding: 64px 24px; } }
    </style>
  </head>
  <body class="propellant-text">
    <section class="propellant-section-navy propellant-notch">
      <div class="content">
        <img
          src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/masschallenge/propellant-web@v2.0.0/assets/logos/masschallenge-logo-horizontal-white.png"
          alt="MassChallenge"
          height="32"
        />
        <p class="propellant-eyebrow">Your eyebrow</p>
        <h1 class="propellant-headline">
          Your lead phrase <span class="propellant-headline-accent">your payoff</span>
        </h1>
        <p class="propellant-body">One or two sentences that say why this page matters.</p>
        <div class="cards">
          <div class="propellant-card">
            <h2 class="propellant-subhead">A card title</h2>
            <p class="propellant-body">A short card text.</p>
          </div>
          <div class="propellant-card">
            <h2 class="propellant-subhead">Another card</h2>
            <p class="propellant-body">A short card text.</p>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="actions">
          <a class="propellant-button" href="#">Your main action</a>
        </div>
      </div>
    </section>
    <section class="propellant-section-angled">
      <div class="content">
        <h2 class="propellant-headline">A section headline</h2>
        <p class="propellant-body">
          Body text with a <a class="propellant-link" href="#">link</a>.
        </p>
        <div class="numbered">
          <div class="propellant-numbered">
            <span class="propellant-numbered-number">01</span>
            <h3 class="propellant-subhead">First step</h3>
            <p class="propellant-body">What happens first.</p>
          </div>
          <div class="propellant-numbered">
            <span class="propellant-numbered-number">02</span>
            <h3 class="propellant-subhead">Second step</h3>
            <p class="propellant-body">What happens next.</p>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="actions">
          <a class="propellant-button" href="#">Primary action</a>
          <a class="propellant-button propellant-button-secondary" href="#">Second choice</a>
        </div>
      </div>
    </section>
  </body>
</html>
```

A similar finished page is in
[`examples/website.html`](https://github.com/masschallenge/propellant-web/blob/v2.0.0/examples/website.html).

## Part 4: Use the colors in your own CSS

Every color in the [website spec](/web/websites/) is also available by name, so your own CSS stays
in step with Propellant:

| Spec color | Use in CSS |
| --- | --- |
| White | `var(--gray-0)` |
| Warm White | `var(--mc-warm-white)` |
| Light tint | `var(--mc-light-tint)` |
| Navy | `var(--mc-navy)` |
| Black | `var(--mc-black)` |
| Deep Teal | `var(--mc-deep-teal)` |
| Teal | `var(--mc-teal)` |
| Cyan | `var(--mc-cyan)` |
| MC Blue | `var(--mc-blue)` |
| Yellow | `var(--mc-yellow)` |
| Slate | `var(--gray-500)` |
| Line | `var(--gray-100)` |
| The MC Gradient | `var(--mc-gradient)` |

```css
.panel {
  background: var(--mc-warm-white);
  border-top: 6px solid var(--mc-black);
  padding: var(--space-6);
}
```

Keep corners square on anything that is not a button.

## Check your work

- Headlines, eyebrows, subheads and buttons are in Oswald capitals. Paragraphs are in Lato, in
  sentence case.
- On light sections, buttons are Teal pills with White text, and hovering clears the fill to a
  Teal outline.
- On dark sections, text is White, accents are Cyan, and buttons are Cyan outlines that fill with
  Teal on hover.
- Cards and photos have square corners.
- Dark and light sections alternate, with a notch where they meet.
- The page reads well on a phone.

## If something looks off

- **Fonts did not change.** Check that the link is inside `<head>` and the address ends in
  `dist/website.css`. Open the address in a browser: you should see CSS, not an error.
- **A button looks like a plain link.** Check the class is spelled `propellant-button`.
- **Your own CSS is ignored.** Load your stylesheet after the Propellant link, so yours comes last.

# HubSpot

Source: https://propellant.masschallenge.org/web/websites/hubspot/

This guide takes a HubSpot website or landing page (Content Hub) from its default look to the
MassChallenge look: Oswald headlines and Lato text, the brand palette, pill shaped Oswald buttons,
and dark Navy sections alternating with White and Warm White ones. Almost all of it happens in
HubSpot's theme settings, with no code. Plan on about an
hour for the settings and logo, and a little longer if you also build a sample page.

We wrote the steps for Elevate, HubSpot's current default theme, because most new HubSpot sites
start on it. If your site uses another theme, the same ideas apply, but the setting names will
differ: a theme only shows the settings its developer built in.

## Before you start

**Your plan.** Theme settings, the brand kit, the drag and drop editor and the mobile view are
available on every HubSpot plan, including the free tools. Custom code is different:

| What | Where it lives | Which plans |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Theme settings, brand kit, section styles | The page editor and Marketing, then Brand | All plans |
| Site header HTML (code added to every page) | Settings, Content, Pages | Varies by plan. HubSpot says not every account can edit it. Check your account. |
| A child theme with its own CSS file | Design Manager | All plans. Free tools and Content Hub Starter allow one child theme, Professional five, Enterprise ten. |
| Attaching a stylesheet to a page or a whole domain | Page settings, or Settings, Content, Pages | Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise, and not for most theme templates (see Part 4) |

**Your permissions.** To change the brand kit you need to be a Super Admin or have the Edit account
defaults permission. To change site wide code you need the Website settings permission.

**Keep the spec open.** Every value in this guide comes from the
[website spec](/web/websites/). Keep it open in another tab so you can copy hex codes from it.

**Download the logo files.** Save these from our logo folder to your computer:

- https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/masschallenge/propellant-web@v2.0.0/assets/logos/masschallenge-logo-horizontal-color.png
  (the main logo, for White and Warm White backgrounds)
- https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/masschallenge/propellant-web@v2.0.0/assets/logos/masschallenge-logo-horizontal-white.png
  (for Navy, Black and Deep Teal backgrounds)
- https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/masschallenge/propellant-web@v2.0.0/assets/logos/masschallenge-logo-monogram-color.png
  (the MC monogram, for the site icon)

The monogram also comes in `-white` and `-black` versions. Read the
[logo rules](/brand/reference/#logo) before you place it: never stretch, recolor or redraw it.

## How HubSpot's style settings fit together

HubSpot has two places for your look, and it helps to know what each one does.

- **The brand kit** (Marketing, then Brand) holds your logo, site icon, brand colors and brand
  fonts. HubSpot uses these across its tools: the logo fills the header, and the colors show up as
  swatches in every color picker.
- **Theme settings** decide how your pages actually look: the fonts for each heading, the colors of
  each section type, and the shape and colors of each button. A change here updates every page that
  uses the theme.

**Which one wins.** Your theme settings decide what visitors see. A theme can use the brand kit
values as its starting point, but once you set a value in theme settings, that value is what the
page shows. Elevate's colors and fonts do not follow the brand kit at all, so set them in both
places: the brand kit for the swatches and the logo, theme settings for the pages. And if one page
looks different from the rest, check that page's own styles, because a style set on a single page
or module beats the theme.

**How Elevate handles color.** Elevate has six palette colors (three base colors and three accent
colors) and four section types: Light section 1, Light section 2, Light section 3 and Dark section 1.
Each section type has its own background, text, caption and link colors. Modules such as Heading
then have a Text color option that picks which section type's colors to use.

## Part 1: Set up site styles (no code)

### Step 1: Fill in the brand kit

1. Click **More** in the top bar, then go to **Marketing**, then **Brand**. (If you do not see
   More, go straight to Marketing, then Brand.)
2. Stay on the **Brand Kit** tab.
3. Under brand colors, click **Edit Colors** and enter these hex codes in each box:

   | Brand kit slot | Spec color | Hex |
   | --- | --- | --- |
   | Primary | Teal | `#00708E` |
   | Secondary | Navy | `#10263F` |
   | Accent 1 | Cyan | `#54EEFF` |
   | Accent 2 | Deep Teal | `#004F73` |
   | Accent 3 | Warm White | `#F8F8F5` |
   | Additional | Black | `#222222` |
   | Additional | Light tint | `#F3FAFC` |
   | Additional | MC Blue | `#0EABBC` |
   | Additional | Slate | `#4B575B` |
   | Additional | Line | `#DBE1E3` |
   | Additional | Yellow | `#FFC801` |
   | Additional | Error | `#BF0261` |

   Click **Add** to make each additional color. Click **Save**.

4. In the **Fonts** section, click **Edit** next to each font and pick **Lato** for the main or
   body font and **Oswald** for the heading or display font, then save. Your account may label
   these two fonts differently; the rule is Oswald for headlines, eyebrows, subheads and buttons,
   and Lato for reading text.
5. Leave this tab open. You will add the logo here in Part 2.

### Step 2: Open the theme settings

You can reach theme settings from any page that uses your theme.

1. Go to **Content**, then **Website Pages** (or **Landing Pages**), and click the name of any
   page to open the editor.
2. Open the theme settings in one of two ways:
   - Click the **Global theme styles** icon in the left sidebar (pages only), or
   - Click the **Edit** menu in the toolbar and choose **Theme**.
3. You will see groups you can expand. In Elevate they are under **Foundation** (Fonts and Colors)
   and **Elements** (Buttons, Links, Forms, Cards and Tags).

You can also get here from the brand kit: next to your active theme, click **Edit / Preview**.

Nothing goes live until you click **Publish theme** (or **Publish** in the universal editor), and
publishing updates every page that uses the theme.

### Step 3: Set the palette colors

Open **Foundation**, then **Colors**. Enter these:

| Elevate setting | Spec color | Hex | What Elevate uses it for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Base color 1 | White | `#FFFFFF` | Page background (Light section 1) |
| Base color 2 | Warm White | `#F8F8F5` | Alternate background (Light section 2) |
| Base color 3 | Black | `#222222` | Text |
| Accent color 1 | Light tint | `#F3FAFC` | Tinted background (Light section 3) |
| Accent color 2 | Cyan | `#54EEFF` | Accents on dark sections |
| Accent color 3 | Teal | `#00708E` | Headings, buttons and links on light |

### Step 4: Set the section colors

Still in **Colors**, open **More settings**, then **Sections**. Use **Choose section to edit** to
switch between the four section types, and enter these values for each:

| Setting | Light section 1 | Light section 2 | Light section 3 | Dark section 1 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Section background color | White `#FFFFFF` | Warm White `#F8F8F5` | Light tint `#F3FAFC` | Navy `#10263F` |
| Default text color | Black `#222222` | Black `#222222` | Black `#222222` | White `#FFFFFF` |
| Accent text color | Teal `#00708E` | Teal `#00708E` | Teal `#00708E` | Cyan `#54EEFF` |
| Caption text color | Slate `#4B575B` | Slate `#4B575B` | Slate `#4B575B` | White `#FFFFFF` |
| Link colors | Primary | Primary | Primary | Secondary |

Elevate's Dark section 1 starts out using Base color 3 (now Black) as its background, so change its
background to Navy here. Navy is the main dark section. For a Black or Deep Teal section, use Dark
section 1 and change only that section's background (Part 3). Never put Teal text on a dark
section.

### Step 5: Set the fonts and text styles

Open **Foundation**, then **Fonts**.

1. Set **Base font** to **Lato**. Every paragraph starts from this font.
2. Open **Font elements**, then **Headings** and **Body**, and set each style:

   | Elevate setting | Spec style | Font | Weight | Size | Color |
   | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   | Heading 1 (H1) | Heading 1 (the headline) | Oswald | 600 (SemiBold) | 64px | Default text color |
   | Heading 2 (H2) | Heading 2 | Oswald | 600 (SemiBold) | 40px | Accent text color |
   | Heading 3 (H3) | Heading 3 (subhead) | Oswald | 600 (SemiBold) | 30px | Accent text color |
   | Heading 4 (H4) | Heading 4 | Oswald | 600 (SemiBold) | 24px | Accent text color |
   | Heading 5 (H5) | Eyebrow | Oswald | 400 (Regular) | 14px | Default text color |
   | Paragraph | Paragraph | Lato | 400 (Regular) | 17px | Default text color |

   If your theme has no color per heading, leave them on the default text color. Headings 2 to 4
   are Teal in the spec, but Black still reads well.

3. Under **Other elements**, open **Caption** and set it to Lato, 400 (Regular), 14px, and set
   **Case** to **None** (Elevate's captions start in capitals, and the spec keeps reading text in
   sentence case).
4. Leave Heading 6 and Block quote alone. The spec does not use them. Heading 5 becomes the eyebrow,
   the small label above a headline, once the Part 4 snippet adds its capitals and letter spacing.

Elevate's font settings have no line height, letter spacing or capitals option for headings.
Headings get a line height of 1.2 and paragraphs 1.55, which is close to the spec. The thing you
will notice is the capitals: every heading, eyebrow and button is in capitals in the spec. You can
either type them in capitals or add the small snippet in Part 4. We recommend the snippet: you keep
typing in sentence case, and the capitals come from the style, which is how the brand works
everywhere else and what screen readers expect.

### Step 6: Set the buttons

Open **Elements**, then **Buttons**. Elevate has four button styles. Use three of them:

| Setting | Primary button | Secondary button | Accent button (for dark sections) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Background | Filled | Outline, or Filled if there is no Outline | Outline, or Filled if there is no Outline |
| Shape | pill | pill | pill |
| Border | 2px | 2px | 2px |
| Default state: Fill color | Teal `#00708E` | White `#FFFFFF` (if Filled) | Navy `#10263F` (if Filled) |
| Default state: Border color | Teal `#00708E` | Teal `#00708E` | Cyan `#54EEFF` |
| Default state: Text color | White `#FFFFFF` | Teal `#00708E` | White `#FFFFFF` |
| Hover state: Fill color | White `#FFFFFF` | Teal `#00708E` | Teal `#00708E` |
| Hover state: Border color | Teal `#00708E` | Teal `#00708E` | Teal `#00708E` |
| Hover state: Text color | Teal `#00708E` | White `#FFFFFF` | White `#FFFFFF` |
| Text: Font | Oswald, 600 (SemiBold), 16px | Oswald, 600 (SemiBold), 16px | Oswald, 600 (SemiBold), 16px |

Notes:

- On light sections the primary button's fill clears to a Teal outline on hover, and the secondary
  button does the opposite. On dark sections the Accent button is a Cyan outline that fills with
  Teal on hover.
- Elevate's primary button text starts out using Base color 2, which is now Warm White, so set it
  to White explicitly.
- Leave the **Tertiary button** unused. If you want it tidy, give it the same values as the
  Secondary button.
- Elevate has no separate corner radius number: **pill** gives fully rounded ends, which is what
  the spec asks for. Other themes may show a **Corner radius** field instead; set it to a large
  number such as 100px for a pill. Never use square corners: square cornered buttons are retired.
- When you add a button to a page, pick **Medium** for **Button size**. Elevate does not show the
  exact padding, so compare it by eye with the spec (about 14px top and bottom, 28px left and
  right).

Type every button label in sentence case, such as Apply now, and add the Part 4 snippet for the
capitals. Without the snippet, type the label in capitals.

### Step 7: Set links, forms and cards

1. **Links, Primary links.** Default state: Text color Teal `#00708E`, turn on **Show underline**,
   Underline color Teal `#00708E`. Hover state: Text color Deep Teal `#004F73`, Show underline on,
   Underline color Deep Teal `#004F73`.
2. **Links, Secondary links** (used on dark sections). Default state: Text color Cyan `#54EEFF`,
   Show underline on, Underline color Cyan `#54EEFF`. Hover state: Text color White `#FFFFFF`, Show
   underline on, Underline color White `#FFFFFF`.
3. **Forms.** Set the field border color and the form border color to Line `#DBE1E3`, and the
   label text color and input text color to Black `#222222`.
4. **Cards.** For each card variant you use, set **Card shape** to **Square**, the background to
   White `#FFFFFF` and the border color to Line `#DBE1E3`. Cards and photos have square corners.
5. Click **Publish theme**.

### Step 8: Check the mobile sizes

HubSpot's editor has a desktop icon and a mobile icon at the top of the screen. Click the mobile
icon to see the phone layout.

Elevate does not have separate mobile font settings. On screens narrower than about 767px it
shrinks every heading to 80% of its desktop size automatically:

| Style | Desktop (you set) | Elevate on phones | Spec on phones |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Heading 1 | 64px | about 51px | 40px |
| Heading 2 | 40px | 32px | 30px |
| Heading 3 | 30px | 24px | 24px |
| Heading 4 | 24px | about 19px | 20px |
| Paragraph | 17px | 17px | 16px |

Heading 3 is exact and the others are close. If you want the phone sizes to match the spec
exactly, the Part 4 snippet does it. The biggest gap is Heading 1, which can wrap awkwardly on a
phone at 51px.

## Part 2: Add the logo and site icon

### The logo

1. Go back to **Marketing**, then **Brand**, **Brand Kit** tab.
2. Click **Add logo +**, then **Upload**, and choose `masschallenge-logo-horizontal-color.png`.
3. Enter **MassChallenge** as the **Logo name** and **MassChallenge** as the **Logo alt text**
   (the words screen readers say and search engines read).
4. In **Link**, enter your home page address so the logo takes people home.
5. Choose **Yes** to make it the default logo, and click **Save**.

Elevate's site header uses the brand kit logo by default. To check, open any page, click the site
header, and look at its **Logo** field. If your header has a Navy, Black or Deep Teal
background, change that one header's logo to `masschallenge-logo-horizontal-white.png`.

Keep the logo at least 24px tall (160px wide), and leave clear space around it equal to the height
of the "M" in the MASSCHALLENGE wordmark, on every side. Align it to a corner or the top edge of the
header. If the header is so small that the horizontal logo would drop below 24px, use the monogram
instead.

### The site icon (favicon)

The favicon is the small icon in the browser tab.

1. In the same **Brand Kit** tab, click **Add Favicon +**.
2. Upload `masschallenge-logo-monogram-color.png`.
3. Name it **MassChallenge monogram**, choose **Yes** to make it the default, and click **Save**.

The favicon only applies to pages hosted on HubSpot.

## Part 3: Build on brand pages

Everything below uses the drag and drop editor. Each page is made of **sections**, which hold
**rows**, which hold **columns** of **modules** (Heading, Rich text, Button, Image and so on).

### Make a light or dark section

1. In the page editor, click the section you want to style. (Hover over the section and click its
   edge, or click its name in the **Contents** tab of the left sidebar.)
2. Open the **Styles** tab in the sidebar.
3. Under **Background**, choose **Color** and enter the hex code:
   - White section: `#FFFFFF`
   - Warm White section: `#F8F8F5`
   - Navy section: `#10263F`
   - Black section: `#222222`
   - Deep Teal section: `#004F73`
4. Under **Alignment and spacing**, set the top and bottom padding to **96px**.
5. Click the **mobile** icon at the top of the editor, select the same section, and set the top and
   bottom padding to **64px**. Changes you make in the mobile view only apply to phones.

Rows and columns have their own background settings too. Keep backgrounds on the section, so the
whole band changes color edge to edge.

**Text inside a dark section.** For each Heading or Rich text module in a Navy, Black or Deep Teal
section, open its **Styles** tab and set **Text color** to **Dark section text color**. That gives
you White text, Cyan accents and the Cyan secondary links you set in Part 1. On White and Warm
White sections, leave it on **Light section 1 text color** (or Light section 2).

Alternate dark and light sections down the page: a Navy opening, a White or Warm White section, a
Navy section with white cards, and so on. The notch between sections and the angled tint on light
sections need code: the Propellant stylesheet at the end of Part 4 has them.

**Hero with a photo.** Under **Background**, choose **Image** and pick a photo by the
[images guide](/guidelines/images/#brand-photography). If your theme offers a background overlay, use a
gradient from Navy black `#051925` on the text side to Ocean `#037AA6` on the subject side, at 15 to
30% opacity. Put text only on a calm area of the photo; otherwise set the section to a solid Navy,
Black or Deep Teal color instead.

**Photos and cards.** Keep image corners square. Use the Card variants you set in Step 7 for white
cards on dark sections.

### Add the eyebrow and the headline

1. Drag a **Heading** module into the top section for the eyebrow. Set **Semantic heading level**
   to **Paragraph** if it is offered (otherwise Heading 5) and **Heading style** to **Heading 5**.
2. Drag a second **Heading** module below it and type the headline in sentence case, for example:
   Build what comes next.
3. Set **Semantic heading level** to **Heading 1**. This tells search engines and screen readers it
   is the main headline.
4. In the **Styles** tab, set **Heading style** to **Heading 1**.
5. For a two toned headline, use a Rich text module instead, select the payoff words, and color
   them Teal `#00708E` on light sections or Cyan `#54EEFF` on dark ones.

Use one Heading 1 per page. Use Heading 2 for each section headline below it, and Heading 3 for card
titles and numbered blocks.

### Add buttons

1. Drag a **Button** module into a column.
2. Enter the **Button text** in sentence case and choose the **Link**.
3. In the **Styles** tab, set **Button style**:
   - **Primary** for the main action on a White or Warm White section.
   - **Secondary** for a second, quieter action next to it.
   - **Accent** for any button on a dark section (a Cyan outline with White text).
4. Set **Button size** to **Medium**.

### Build a sample home page

1. **Opening band.** A Navy section, with a photo if you have a good one. Add the eyebrow, a Heading
   module (Heading 1, Dark section text color) and a Rich text paragraph below it, also on Dark
   section text color. Add a Button module with the Accent style.
2. **What we do.** A Warm White section. A Heading 2, a paragraph of no more than about 720px wide
   (set the column narrower, or use a two column row and leave one empty), and a Primary button.
3. **Three cards.** A Navy section with a row of three columns, each a white card with an image, a
   Heading 3 and a short paragraph.
4. **Final call to action.** A White section with a Heading 2, a Primary button and a Secondary
   button side by side.
5. Click the mobile icon and check each section before you publish.

## Part 4: Custom CSS (optional, only what settings cannot do)

You can stop at Part 3. Add code only if you want these things, which Elevate's settings cannot
do:

- **Capitals** on every heading and button, with a line height of 1.0 on Heading 1 and Heading 2.
  Elevate has no case, letter spacing or line height setting for headings.
- **The eyebrow**: Heading 5 in Oswald Regular with letter spacing of 0.3em.
- **Exact phone sizes** for Heading 1, Heading 2, Heading 4 and paragraphs. Elevate only shrinks
  headings by a fixed 80%.
- **Exact line heights** for Heading 3 (1.1), Heading 4 (1.15) and paragraphs (1.5).

The snippet targets Elevate's own heading tags, its `hs-elevate-h1` style names and its buttons, so
it only touches headings, buttons and body text.

### Option A: Site header HTML (simplest)

This adds the code to the top of every page on a domain. Whether your plan includes it varies, so
look for the field in your account.

1. Click the **settings** icon (the gear) in the top bar.
2. In the left sidebar, go to **Content**, then **Pages**.
3. In **Choose a domain to edit its settings**, pick your website's domain, or **Default settings
   for all domains**.
4. Find **Site header HTML**. (In some accounts it sits on a tab called **Templates**.) If you
   picked one domain and the field is locked, click **Override default settings**.
5. Paste this at the end of whatever is already in the field:

   ```html
   <style>
     /* Propellant website styles: see github.com/masschallenge/propellant-web */
     body :is(h1, h2, h3, h4, h5),
     body :is(.hs-elevate-h1, .hs-elevate-h2, .hs-elevate-h3, .hs-elevate-h4, .hs-elevate-h5),
     body .hs-elevate-button {
       text-transform: uppercase;
     }
     body h1,
     body .hs-elevate-h1,
     body h2,
     body .hs-elevate-h2 {
       line-height: 1;
     }
     body h3,
     body .hs-elevate-h3 {
       line-height: 1.1;
     }
     body h4,
     body .hs-elevate-h4 {
       line-height: 1.15;
     }
     body h5,
     body .hs-elevate-h5 {
       letter-spacing: 0.3em;
     }
     body .hs-elevate-button {
       letter-spacing: 0.05em;
     }
     html body {
       line-height: 1.5;
     }
     @media (max-width: 766px) {
       body h1,
       body .hs-elevate-h1 {
         font-size: 40px;
       }
       body h2,
       body .hs-elevate-h2 {
         font-size: 30px;
       }
       body h4,
       body .hs-elevate-h4 {
         font-size: 20px;
       }
       html body {
         font-size: 16px;
       }
     }
   </style>
   ```

6. Click **Save** in the bottom left.

To see a single page with the code before you add it everywhere, open that page, go to the
**Settings** menu, then **Advanced**, and paste it into **Head HTML** under **Additional code
snippets** instead.

**To remove it later**, open the same field and delete everything from `<style>` to `</style>`,
then save. Leave any other code in the field alone (it is often tracking code someone else added).

### Option B: A child theme

A child theme is a copy of Elevate that keeps getting Elevate's updates, plus an empty CSS file of
its own. Use this if your plan does not include Site header HTML, or if you prefer to keep styles
with the theme.

1. Go to **Content**, then **Design Manager**.
2. Open the **@hubspot** folder, right click the **elevate** folder and choose **Create child
   theme**. (Elevate itself cannot be cloned, so a child theme is the way to change it.)
3. Give it a name, such as MassChallenge, and click **Create child theme**.
4. Open the new theme's CSS file (named `child.css` unless you renamed it) and paste the snippet
   from Option A **without** the `<style>` and `</style>` lines. Click **Publish changes**.
5. Build new pages with the child theme's templates. Existing pages keep their old theme until you
   swap each page's template to the matching child theme template.
6. Open theme settings on a child theme page and check your Part 1 values. The child theme starts
   from Elevate's settings, so you may need to enter them again there.

**To remove it later**, delete the snippet from the CSS file and click **Publish changes**.

### Option C: Attached stylesheets (usually not for Elevate)

HubSpot can also attach a CSS file from the Design Manager to one page (page **Settings**, then
**Advanced**, then **Stylesheets**) or to a whole domain (**Settings**, **Content**, **Pages**,
**CSS & Stylesheets**). Both need Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise, and neither works on
Elevate's templates: page stylesheets are not available for theme templates, and domain stylesheets
only work on theme templates built to accept them. Use Option A or B instead.

### Using the Propellant stylesheet instead

The [Propellant stylesheet](/web/websites/#the-propellant-stylesheet) loads Lato and Oswald and
adds ready made classes that match the spec: `propellant-headline` is Heading 1 (including the
capitals and the 40px phone size), `propellant-eyebrow` is the eyebrow, `propellant-title-1`,
`propellant-subhead` and `propellant-title-3` are Heading 2, 3 and 4, `propellant-body` is
Paragraph, and `propellant-caption` is Paragraph small in Slate. It also has the patterns that
sections cannot do on their own: `propellant-notch` for the notch below a section,
`propellant-section-angled` for the angled tint, and `propellant-hero` for the hero overlay. To load it, paste this line into Site header
HTML (Option A) on its own, outside any `<style>` tags:

```html
<link
  rel="stylesheet"
  href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/masschallenge/propellant-web@v2.0.0/dist/website.css"
/>
```

It only styles elements you give a class to, so it changes nothing on its own. In HubSpot you add a
class by editing the HTML of a Rich text module (its source code view), for example:

```html
<h1 class="propellant-headline">Build what comes next</h1>
```

For most HubSpot sites the theme settings plus the Option A snippet are simpler, because you
keep editing in HubSpot's own modules. For buttons, keep using the Button module with the styles
from Part 1: Elevate styles every plain link on the page, and its link color rule can win over
a `propellant-button` class placed inside a Rich text module. To remove the stylesheet, delete the
`<link ... />` line.

## Check your work

On desktop:

- [ ] Headings, eyebrows and buttons are in Oswald, and paragraphs are in Lato.
- [ ] Headings and buttons show in capitals (with the snippet); paragraphs are in sentence case.
- [ ] Body text is Black, captions are Slate, and links are Teal and underlined on light sections
      and Cyan on dark ones.
- [ ] Primary buttons are Teal pills with White text that clear to a Teal outline on hover.
- [ ] Secondary buttons are Teal outlines with Teal text.
- [ ] Dark sections have White text, Cyan outline buttons, and no Teal text.
- [ ] Dark and light sections alternate down the page.
- [ ] Cards and images have square corners.
- [ ] The full color logo sits in the header and links home; the favicon shows the monogram.

On a phone (use the editor's mobile icon, then check the published page on a real phone):

- [ ] Heading 1 fits without awkward wrapping.
- [ ] Sections have about 64px of space above and below.
- [ ] Buttons are easy to tap and their labels fit on one line.

## If something looks off

- **One page ignores the theme.** That page or module has its own style set. Select the module or
  section, open its **Styles** tab, and clear the override (for example set Background back to
  **None**).
- **Headings are still in the old font.** You changed the brand kit but not the theme. Set the fonts
  in theme settings (Part 1, Step 5) and click **Publish theme**.
- **Text on a dark section is hard to read.** The module is still on a light text color. Set its
  **Text color** to **Dark section text color**.
- **Primary button text is pale gray instead of White.** Set **Primary button**, **Default state**,
  **Text color** to `#FFFFFF`; Elevate starts it on Base color 2.
- **The snippet does nothing.** Check that you saved the domain you are viewing (or Default
  settings for all domains), that the code sits between `<style>` and `</style>`, and look at the
  published page rather than the editor preview.
- **A theme update changed something.** Open theme settings and compare each value with the
  [spec](/web/websites/). Settings are the source of truth; change them there rather than adding
  more code.

# Squarespace

Source: https://propellant.masschallenge.org/web/websites/squarespace/

This guide takes a Squarespace 7.1 site, new or existing, and gives it the MassChallenge look:
Lato text, Oswald headlines in capitals, the brand palette, pill shaped Oswald buttons, and dark
Navy and Deep Teal sections alternating with White and Warm White ones. Most of it is point and
click in Squarespace's own style settings. One optional step adds a few lines of code for the
eyebrow and the button hovers. Plan on about an hour the first time, and less once you know where
things live.

All of the steps are for Squarespace version 7.1, the current version. If your site is on version
7.0, the menus are different and this guide will not match. To check, open the **Pages** panel
and look at the bottom: Squarespace shows your site's version there.

## Before you start

**Your plan.** Most of this guide works on every Squarespace plan. The code steps depend on your
plan:

| What | Where it lives | Plans that allow it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Custom CSS (small pieces of style code) | Pages panel, **Custom Code**, **Custom CSS** | All plans |
| Code injection (code added to the head of every page) | Pages panel, **Custom Code**, **Code Injection** | Core, Plus, Advanced and some older (legacy) plans |

You only need Custom CSS for this guide, so any plan will do. Code injection is an alternative for
one step, and it is only on Core and above.

**Keep the spec open.** Every value you will type comes from the [website spec](/web/websites/).
Keep it open in another tab so you can copy hex codes from it.

**Download the logo files.** Use these files only, never a copy from somewhere else. Open each link
and save the image to your computer:

- Full color horizontal logo, for the header on White:
  https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/masschallenge/propellant-web@v2.0.0/assets/logos/masschallenge-logo-horizontal-color.png
- White horizontal logo, for Navy, Black and Deep Teal backgrounds:
  https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/masschallenge/propellant-web@v2.0.0/assets/logos/masschallenge-logo-horizontal-white.png
- Full color monogram (the MC mark on its own), for the browser icon:
  https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/masschallenge/propellant-web@v2.0.0/assets/logos/masschallenge-logo-monogram-color.png
- There are also `-white` and `-black` versions of the monogram, and a `-black` horizontal logo,
  at the same address with the color word changed. The [brand guidelines](/brand/reference/) say when to
  use each one.

**One habit that saves trouble.** In Squarespace, style settings apply to the whole site. If you
change a font size or color with the text toolbar inside a single block, that block stops
following the site settings. Set things once in Site styles and leave the toolbar for choosing a
format such as Heading 2.

## Part 1: Set up site styles (no code)

This is the main part of the guide. You will set fonts, colors and buttons once, and every page
picks them up.

### Open Site styles

1. Open the **Pages** panel and click any page.
2. Click the **paintbrush** icon in the top right corner. The **Site styles** panel opens.
3. You will see sections such as **Fonts**, **Colors**, **Buttons** and **Spacing**. Click the
   **>** arrow next to a section to open its settings.

Two warnings before you start:

- Site styles has a **Themes** option, and Fonts and Buttons each offer ready made **packs**.
  Picking a theme or a pack replaces your fonts, colors or buttons in one go. Once you have set
  things up, do not click a different theme or pack. If you do by accident, use the **undo** arrow
  at the top of the panel.
- Click **Save** at the top of the editor when you finish each section, so nothing is lost.

### Step 1: Fonts

How Squarespace fonts work, in plain words: text comes in four groups, **Headings**,
**Paragraphs**, **Buttons** and **Miscellaneous** (small extras such as dates and captions). Each
group has one font for the whole group. Inside Headings there are four sizes, Heading 1 to Heading
4. Inside Paragraphs there are three sizes, Paragraph 1 (large), Paragraph 2 (normal) and
Paragraph 3 (small). Sizes are set in **rem**, which means "times the base size". With a base size
of 16, 2rem is 32 pixels.

That one font per group suits the spec: every heading is Oswald SemiBold in capitals, and every
paragraph is Lato. The one style Squarespace cannot set on its own is the eyebrow, the small
tracked label above a headline, because it needs a lighter weight and wide letter spacing. Part 4
adds a few lines of code that turn Heading 4 into the eyebrow. If you skip Part 4, use Heading 4 as
a small subhead instead.

**Choose a starting font pack**

1. In Site styles, click **Fonts**.
2. If you want, click **>** next to Fonts, then **All Font Packs**, then **Sans-serif**, and pick
   any pack. It does not matter which: you are about to change every font in it. If your site
   already has a pack, skip this.

**Set the base size**

1. Click **>** next to **Fonts**.
2. Use the **+** and **-** buttons to set the **Base size** to **16**. Every size below assumes a
   base of 16.

**Headings**

Click **Headings** and set:

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Font | **Oswald** (type "Oswald" in the font search) |
| Style or weight | **600** (SemiBold) |
| Line height | **1.0em** (see the note below) |
| Letter spacing | **0em** |
| Text transform | **Uppercase** |

Then set each size:

| Squarespace size | Spec style | Desktop size in the spec | Enter |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Heading 1 | Heading 1 (the headline) | 64px | **4rem** |
| Heading 2 | Heading 2 | 40px | **2.5rem** |
| Heading 3 | Heading 3 (subhead) | 30px | **1.875rem** |
| Heading 4 | Eyebrow (with Part 4), or Heading 4 | 14px, or 24px without Part 4 | **0.875rem**, or **1.5rem** without Part 4 |

A note on line height: the spec gives the headlines a line height of 1.0 and the subheads 1.1. If
your panel shows a line height for each heading size, enter 1.0em for Headings 1 and 2 and 1.1em
for Headings 3 and 4. If it shows one line height for all headings, use 1.0em.

If you type a heading in normal sentence case, the capitals come from the Uppercase setting. Keep
typing it that way, so screen readers and search engines read it correctly.

If a slider will not land on an exact value, click the number and type it.

**Paragraphs**

Click **Paragraphs** and set:

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Font | **Lato** |
| Style or weight | **400** (Regular) |
| Line height | **1.5em** |
| Letter spacing | **0em** |
| Text transform | **None** |

Then set each size:

| Squarespace size | Spec style | Desktop size in the spec | Enter |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Paragraph 1 | Paragraph large | 20px | **1.25rem** |
| Paragraph 2 | Paragraph | 17px | **1.0625rem** |
| Paragraph 3 | Paragraph small | 14px | **0.875rem** |

Every paragraph size uses a line height of 1.5em.

**Buttons**

Click **Buttons** (inside Fonts) and set:

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Font | **Oswald** |
| Style or weight | **600** (SemiBold) |
| Size | **1rem** (16px) |
| Letter spacing | **0.05em** |
| Text transform | **Uppercase** |

Buttons are in Oswald capitals. Type the label in sentence case; the capitals come from the
Uppercase setting. If your panel shows separate font settings for Primary, Secondary and Tertiary
buttons, set all three the same way.

**Miscellaneous**

Click **Miscellaneous** and set the font to **Lato**, weight **400**, letter spacing **0em** and
text transform **None**. This covers small text such as dates, so it should match your paragraphs.

**If Lato is not in the list**

Squarespace's library holds hundreds of Google Fonts but not every one. Lato should be there; if
your search finds nothing, you can upload it:

1. Download Lato from Google Fonts (fonts.google.com, search "Lato"). You need the Regular (400)
   and Bold (700) files.
2. In Site styles, click **>** next to Fonts, then click **Headings** (or Paragraphs).
3. Click the font dropdown, then click the **upload** icon.
4. Drag in one font file, or click **+** and choose it. Upload each weight as its own file.
   Squarespace accepts .otf, .ttf, .woff and .woff2 files.
5. Your fonts appear under **Uploaded** in every font dropdown. Choose Lato there.

Oswald is in the library too. If your search does not find it, upload it the same way, with the
Regular (400), SemiBold (600) and Bold (700) files.

### Step 2: Colors

How Squarespace colors work, in plain words: there are two layers.

1. **The palette.** Every site has a palette of exactly five colors. They are the starting point
   for everything else.
2. **Color themes.** Squarespace builds ten color themes from the palette. A color theme is a full
   set of colors for one section: its background, headings, paragraphs, links and buttons. You
   give each section of a page one theme. The ten themes are named from lightest to darkest:
   **Lightest 1**, **Lightest 2**, **Light 1**, **Light 2**, **Bright 1**, **Bright 2**,
   **Dark 1**, **Dark 2**, **Darkest 1** and **Darkest 2**.

Inside a theme you can pick any color for any part, either one of the five palette colors or a
**Custom** color you type in. That is how you get colors such as Deep Teal and Cyan, which do not
fit in a five color palette.

We use five themes, one for each kind of section in the spec:

| Section in the spec | Squarespace theme |
| --- | --- |
| White (the normal page background) | **Lightest 1** |
| Warm White (the alternate light section) | **Light 1** |
| Navy (the main dark section) | **Darkest 1** |
| Black (a dark section) | **Darkest 2** |
| Deep Teal (a dark section) | **Dark 1** |

**Edit the palette**

1. In Site styles, click **>** next to **Colors**.
2. Click **Edit palette**.
3. Click each of the five colors in turn and type its hex code into the value field, so the palette
   matches this table from lightest to darkest:

| Palette position | Spec color | Hex |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 (lightest) | White | `#FFFFFF` |
| 2 | Warm White | `#F8F8F5` |
| 3 | Teal | `#00708E` |
| 4 | Navy | `#10263F` |
| 5 (darkest) | Black | `#222222` |

4. Click **Save**.

Changing the palette can change your color themes too, so always edit the palette first and the
themes second. If you edit the palette again later, check your five themes afterwards.

**Edit the five color themes**

For each of the five themes below:

1. In the Colors panel, click the theme (for example **Lightest 1**).
2. Click a part, such as **Background**. Pick from the **Palette** tab, or click **Custom** and type
   the hex code.
3. Work through every part in the table.
4. Click **Save**.

The exact names of the parts can differ slightly from site to site. Squarespace calls the four
heading sizes Heading (Extra Large), Heading (Large), Heading (Medium) and Heading (Small): they
are Heading 1 to Heading 4. Paragraphs are Paragraph (Large), Paragraph (Medium) and Paragraph
(Small). If you see a part that is not in this table, such as a block's own colors, match it to the
closest row.

Start with the two light themes:

| Part | Lightest 1 (White) | Light 1 (Warm White) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Background | White `#FFFFFF` | Warm White `#F8F8F5` |
| Heading (Extra Large) | Black `#222222` | Black `#222222` |
| Heading (Large), (Medium) and (Small) | Teal `#00708E` | Teal `#00708E` |
| Paragraph (Large) and (Medium) | Black `#222222` | Black `#222222` |
| Paragraph (Small) | Slate `#4B575B` | Slate `#4B575B` |
| Links (paragraph and heading links) | Teal `#00708E` | Teal `#00708E` |
| Primary button background | Teal `#00708E` | Teal `#00708E` |
| Primary button text | White `#FFFFFF` | White `#FFFFFF` |
| Secondary button background | White `#FFFFFF` | Warm White `#F8F8F5` |
| Secondary button text | Teal `#00708E` | Teal `#00708E` |
| Tertiary button background | White `#FFFFFF` | Warm White `#F8F8F5` |
| Tertiary button text | Teal `#00708E` | Teal `#00708E` |
| Lines and dividers | Line `#DBE1E3` | Line `#DBE1E3` |
| Site title and navigation links (if listed) | Black `#222222` | Black `#222222` |

Then the three dark themes. They differ only in their background:

| Part | Darkest 1 (Navy) | Darkest 2 (Black) | Dark 1 (Deep Teal) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Background | Navy `#10263F` | Black `#222222` | Deep Teal `#004F73` |
| All four headings | White `#FFFFFF` | White `#FFFFFF` | White `#FFFFFF` |
| All paragraphs | White `#FFFFFF` | White `#FFFFFF` | White `#FFFFFF` |
| Links (paragraph and heading links) | Cyan `#54EEFF` | Cyan `#54EEFF` | Cyan `#54EEFF` |
| Primary, Secondary and Tertiary button background | Teal `#00708E` | Teal `#00708E` | Teal `#00708E` |
| Primary, Secondary and Tertiary button text | White `#FFFFFF` | White `#FFFFFF` | White `#FFFFFF` |
| Lines and dividers | Cyan `#54EEFF` | Cyan `#54EEFF` | Cyan `#54EEFF` |
| Site title and navigation links (if listed) | White `#FFFFFF` | White `#FFFFFF` | White `#FFFFFF` |

Why the buttons look like this: on light sections the primary button is a solid Teal pill and the
secondary is Teal text on the section's own color. On dark sections the spec asks for a Cyan
outline that fills with Teal on hover. Squarespace has no outline color setting, so the dark themes
show the Teal fill, which is the hover look and is always readable. Snippet B in Part 4 adds the
outlines and the hover behaviors. Squarespace only uses Tertiary buttons in a few places, such as
the cookie banner, so we make them match Secondary.

Never put Teal text on Navy, Black or Deep Teal: it is too dark to read. If you see Teal text in a
dark theme on your screen, change it to White, or to Cyan for links. Cyan is only ever used on the
dark themes.

You can leave the other five themes alone. Just use only these five for your sections. MC Blue is
not set here: it is for the logo and graphic shapes, never text. The warm accents (Yellow, Orange,
Raspberry and Lime) are not set here either: use one per page, in small doses, such as a tag or a
stat in an image.

### Step 3: Buttons

How Squarespace buttons work, in plain words: there are three button types, **Primary**,
**Secondary** and **Tertiary**. Each has its own shape, outline and padding (the space between the
text and the edge of the button). Colors do not live here: they come from the color theme of the
section, which you set in Step 2.

Most buttons on a Squarespace site are Primary. Button blocks, header buttons and form submit
buttons can be switched to Secondary or Tertiary.

1. In Site styles, click **>** next to **Buttons**.
2. Click **Primary** and set:

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Fill | **Fill** (a solid background, sometimes called Solid). Not No Fill. |
| Shape | **Pill** (fully rounded ends) |
| Outline | Slide to **0** (snippet B draws the outline) |
| Padding | Click **...** and set **Top & Bottom** to **14px** and **Left & Right** to **28px** |

3. Click **Font** if you did not set button fonts in Step 1: Oswald, 600, 1rem, letter spacing
   0.05em, text transform Uppercase.
4. Click **Apply to all Button Types**, so Secondary and Tertiary get the same shape and padding.
5. Click **Save**.

If the padding field does not accept pixels, choose **M** and compare the button with the spec:
it should be a little under three times as wide as it is tall for a short label such as "Apply".

If you see shadow or raised options, turn them off. The spec has no shadows. Never choose a square
or rounded rectangle shape: square cornered buttons are retired.

Hover: Squarespace has no setting for what a button does when you point at it. It fades the button
slightly instead. The spec asks for more: on light sections the primary button's fill clears to a
Teal outline, and on dark sections a Cyan outline fills with Teal. Part 4 has a small snippet for
that. It is optional: a faded hover still works.

### Step 4: Spacing

The spec asks for generous space: about 96px above and below each section on desktop and 64px on
phones, and paragraphs about 720px wide. When in doubt, add space.

1. In Site styles, click **Spacing**. You can leave **Site Margin** (the space between your content
   and the edge of the screen) at its default.
2. Section spacing is set on each section, not here. See "Section spacing" in Part 3.

### Step 5: Mobile

Squarespace 7.1 always rearranges and resizes your site for phones, and you cannot turn that off.
There is no separate set of mobile font sizes in Site styles: headings shrink on their own as the
screen gets narrower. The spec's mobile sizes (for example 40px for Heading 1) are close to what
Squarespace does by itself. If your Heading 1 is too big or too small on a phone, Part 4 has a
snippet that sets it to exactly 40px.

To see your phone layout, switch the editor to its mobile view (the phone icon at the top of the
page editor). In Fluid Engine sections (Squarespace's drag and drop grid), you can move and resize
blocks for mobile separately from desktop. Always check every page there before you publish.

## Part 2: Add the logo and site icon

### The logo

1. Click **Edit** in the top left corner of the page.
2. Hover over the header (the strip at the top with your site name) and click **Edit Site Header**.
3. Click the site title or logo, then click the **pencil** icon.
4. In **Logo Image**, click **+**, then **Upload File**, and choose
   `masschallenge-logo-horizontal-color.png`.
5. Use the slider to set the logo height. Keep it at **24px or taller**, so the logo stays at
   least 160px wide and the wordmark stays readable. A height around 32px works well in most
   headers.
6. In **Mobile Logo Image**, upload the same file and use **Mobile Logo Max Height** to keep it at
   least 24px tall.
7. Click **Save**.

Keep the header on a White or Warm White background so the full color logo fits. In **Edit Site
Header**, click **Colors** and choose **Lightest 1** or **Light 1**. If you give the header a Navy,
Black or Deep Teal background, upload `masschallenge-logo-horizontal-white.png` instead: never put
the full color logo on a dark color.

Logo rules from the [brand guidelines](/brand/reference/):

- Keep clear space around the logo equal to the height of the "M" in the MASSCHALLENGE wordmark,
  on every side. Nothing, not even the edge of the header, goes inside it.
- Align the logo to a corner or the top edge of its area.
- Do not stretch, crop, recolor or add effects to it.
- Do not use Squarespace's image editor on the logo. It saves images as .jpg, which turns the
  transparent background white. Upload the .png file as it is.

### The site icon (favicon)

The site icon, or favicon, is the small picture in the browser tab. Use the monogram.

1. Open **Settings**, then **Website**, then **Favicon**. (The help center links straight to this
   panel; on some accounts it is called **Browser icon**.)
2. Drag `masschallenge-logo-monogram-color.png` into the uploader, or click it and choose the file.
3. Optional: add a dark mode version with `masschallenge-logo-monogram-white.png`. You must add the
   normal icon first.
4. Click **Save**.

Squarespace's limits: the file must be .png (recommended), under 100 KB, and works best between
100 and 300 pixels. The monogram file is 321 by 177 pixels and about 6 KB, so it uploads fine.
Because it is wider than it is tall, it shows small in the tab. If it looks squashed, place it in
the middle of a transparent square image (321 by 321 pixels) in any image editor and upload that.

Browsers hold on to old icons. If you still see the old one, clear your browser's cache or open the
site in a private window.

## Part 3: Build on brand pages

### Give each section its color

Every page is made of sections. Give each one a theme:

1. Open the **Pages** panel, click the page, and click **Edit**.
2. Hover over a section and click **Edit Section**.
3. Click **Colors** and choose:
   - **Lightest 1** for a White section,
   - **Light 1** for a Warm White section,
   - **Darkest 1** for a Navy section,
   - **Darkest 2** for a Black section,
   - **Dark 1** for a Deep Teal section.
4. Click **Save**.

Alternate dark and light sections down the page: the brand's rhythm is a dark section, then a light
one, then a dark one. Navy is the main dark section; use Black and Deep Teal for variety.

A theme changes every color in the section, including any color you picked with the text toolbar.
Remember too that editing a theme changes every section on the site that uses it. That is what you
want: change Darkest 1 once and every Navy section follows.

The notch (the small triangle that points down from one section into the next) and the angled tint
on light sections need code that Squarespace sections cannot take. On a Core plan or above you can
build them inside a Code block with the Propellant stylesheet, as shown at the end of Part 4.
Without them, the alternating colors still carry the rhythm.

### Section spacing

1. In **Edit Section**, click **Design** (it may be called **Format**).
2. Leave **Fill Screen** off unless you want a full height section.
3. In a Fluid Engine section, leave about one empty grid row above and below your content, and
   adjust **Row Count** until the space looks like about 96px on desktop. In a classic section, use
   **Section Height** and pick a small or medium height.
4. Keep text blocks to about 720px wide (roughly 68 characters a line). On a normal width page,
   that is a little over half the width of the grid. Long full width paragraphs are hard to read.
5. Check the mobile view: aim for about 64px of space above and below.

Squarespace does not let you type an exact pixel value for section spacing, so judge it by eye.

### Add the headline and text

1. Add a **Text** block.
2. If you added snippet A, start with the eyebrow: type a few words and choose **Heading 4** from
   the format menu in the text toolbar.
3. Type your headline, select it, and choose **Heading 1**. Type it in normal sentence case: the
   capitals come from Site styles, not from your keyboard.
4. For a two toned headline, select the payoff words and click the link color or the text color in
   the toolbar, then choose Teal on light sections or Cyan on dark ones. This is the one place to
   use the toolbar color.
5. Use **Heading 1** once per page, for the headline. Use **Heading 2** for section headlines and
   **Heading 3** for subheads, such as card titles and the titles of numbered blocks.
6. Use **Paragraph 2** for normal text, **Paragraph 1** for a short introduction under the
   headline, and **Paragraph 3** for small print such as dates. Never set paragraphs in capitals.
7. Do not change fonts or sizes with the toolbar. Let Site styles do it.

**Numbered blocks.** For steps or a short list of points, add a **Line** block, then a Text block
with the number (such as 01) as Heading 2, the title as Heading 3 and the text as Paragraph 2. The
number takes the Teal heading color on light sections.

**Photos.** Leave image corners square. In an **Image** block, keep the **Design** option with no
rounded corners. Pick photos by the [images guide](/guidelines/images/#brand-photography).

### Add buttons

1. Add a **Button** block.
2. In the **Content** tab, type the label. Type it in sentence case with a verb, such as "Apply
   now" or "Meet the startups": the capitals come from Site styles.
3. In the **Design** tab, open the **Primary Button** dropdown:
   - Keep **Primary Button** for the main action (a solid Teal pill on light sections).
   - Choose **Secondary Button** for a second, quieter action (Teal text, with a Teal outline if
     you added snippet B).
4. Under **Size**, choose **M**, the size that matches the padding you set in Part 1.
5. In a Fluid Engine section, set the button to **Fit** rather than **Fill**, so it keeps its pill
   shape and padding.

On a dark section, buttons turn Teal with White text on their own, because of the dark themes, and
snippet B turns them into Cyan outlines. Use one primary button there.

### Sample home page

A simple page you can build in about fifteen minutes. Replace the bracketed text with your own.

1. **Hero, Navy (Darkest 1).** A full width Image block or a section background photo, chosen by
   the [images guide](/guidelines/images/#brand-photography). Over a calm area of the photo, a Text block
   with an eyebrow (Heading 4), your headline as Heading 1 and one or two sentences as Paragraph 1.
   Below it, a primary Button block ("[Main action]"). If the text is hard to read over the photo,
   move it to a calm area or set the section without a photo.
2. **What we do, Warm White (Light 1).** A Heading 2 headline. Under it, three short numbered
   blocks, each a Line block, a number, a Heading 3 and a Paragraph 2.
3. **Proof, Navy (Darkest 1).** A Heading 2 headline, then three white cards: in each column, a
   Text block with a Heading 3 title and a Paragraph 2, on a White background (in Fluid Engine,
   click the block, then **Design**, and give it a White background).
4. **Call to action, White (Lightest 1).** A Heading 2 and one sentence in Paragraph 1, with one
   primary Button block.
5. **Footer, Black (Darkest 2).** Edit the footer section and give it **Darkest 2**. Use the white
   logo file there.

## Part 4: Custom CSS (only what settings cannot do)

This part is optional. Your site is already on brand after Parts 1 to 3. Custom CSS is a few lines
of style code that you paste into one box; it adds three things that Squarespace settings cannot
do:

| Snippet | What it fixes | Why settings cannot do it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A: the eyebrow | Heading 4 in Text blocks becomes the eyebrow: Oswald Regular, 14px, capitals, letter spacing 0.3em | All heading sizes share one weight and one letter spacing |
| B: button outlines and hovers | On light sections, the primary fill clears to a Teal outline on hover and the secondary button gets a Teal outline that fills on hover. On dark sections, buttons are Cyan outlines that fill with Teal on hover | There is no outline color or hover setting |
| C: exact headline sizes (optional) | Heading 1 at exactly 64px on desktop and 40px on phones | Squarespace scales headings with the screen, so sizes are close but not exact |

### Where to paste it

1. Open the **Pages** panel.
2. At the bottom, click **Custom Code**, then **Custom CSS**. (On some sites this is under
   **Design**, then **Custom CSS**, or **Website Tools**, then **Custom CSS**.)
3. Paste the snippets into the box. If the box already has code, paste them at the end.
4. Click **Save**.

The Custom CSS panel is available on every plan.

### Snippet A: the eyebrow

```css
/* Propellant website styles: see github.com/masschallenge/propellant-web */
.sqs-block-html h4 {
  font-weight: 400;
  font-size: 14px;
  line-height: 1.2;
  letter-spacing: 0.3em;
}
```

What it does: it styles Heading 4, but only inside Text blocks (that is what `.sqs-block-html`
means), as the eyebrow. The font and the capitals already come from Site styles. Use Heading 4 only
for eyebrows once this snippet is in place.

### Snippet B: button outlines and hovers

```css
/* Propellant website styles: see github.com/masschallenge/propellant-web */
.sqs-button-element--primary,
.sqs-button-element--secondary {
  box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px #00708e;
}

.sqs-button-element--primary:hover {
  background-color: transparent !important;
  color: #00708e !important;
  opacity: 1 !important;
}

.sqs-button-element--secondary:hover {
  background-color: #00708e !important;
  color: #ffffff !important;
  opacity: 1 !important;
}

[data-section-theme="black"] .sqs-button-element--primary,
[data-section-theme="black"] .sqs-button-element--secondary,
[data-section-theme="black-bold"] .sqs-button-element--primary,
[data-section-theme="black-bold"] .sqs-button-element--secondary,
[data-section-theme="dark"] .sqs-button-element--primary,
[data-section-theme="dark"] .sqs-button-element--secondary {
  background-color: transparent !important;
  color: #ffffff !important;
  box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px #54eeff;
}

[data-section-theme="black"] .sqs-button-element--primary:hover,
[data-section-theme="black"] .sqs-button-element--secondary:hover,
[data-section-theme="black-bold"] .sqs-button-element--primary:hover,
[data-section-theme="black-bold"] .sqs-button-element--secondary:hover,
[data-section-theme="dark"] .sqs-button-element--primary:hover,
[data-section-theme="dark"] .sqs-button-element--secondary:hover {
  background-color: #00708e !important;
  color: #ffffff !important;
  box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px #00708e;
}
```

`.sqs-button-element--primary` and `--secondary` are the names Squarespace gives primary and
secondary buttons. The outline is drawn with `box-shadow`, so the button keeps its size.
`!important` makes sure our hover wins over Squarespace's fade. `black`, `black-bold` and `dark`
are the names Squarespace uses behind the scenes for the **Darkest 1**, **Darkest 2** and **Dark
1** themes, so those rules only touch buttons on Navy, Black and Deep Teal sections. If you chose
different themes for your dark sections, these rules will not apply; switch those sections to the
themes in Step 2.

### Snippet C: exact headline sizes (optional)

```css
/* Propellant website styles: see github.com/masschallenge/propellant-web */
.sqs-block-html h1 {
  font-size: 64px;
}

@media (max-width: 767px) {
  .sqs-block-html h1 {
    font-size: 40px;
  }
}
```

The second part applies only on screens 767px wide or narrower, which is where Squarespace switches
to its phone layout.

### Alternative: load the Propellant stylesheet (Core plan and above)

If your plan includes code injection, you can also load the Propellant stylesheet. It loads the
exact Oswald and Lato files we use, and adds ready made classes for the patterns that sections
cannot do on their own, such as the notch, the angled tint and the hero overlay.

1. Open the **Pages** panel, click **Custom Code**, then **Code Injection**.
2. In the **Header** box, paste:

```html
<link
  rel="stylesheet"
  href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/masschallenge/propellant-web@v2.0.0/dist/website.css"
/>
```

3. Click **Save**.

The stylesheet only styles elements that carry one of its class names, so it never changes the
rest of your site. Squarespace's own blocks do not let you add class names, so you use the classes
inside a **Code** block, where you write a little HTML. For example:

```html
<div class="propellant-section-angled">
  <p class="propellant-eyebrow">Your eyebrow</p>
  <h2 class="propellant-headline">Your headline here</h2>
  <a class="propellant-button" href="/apply">Apply now</a>
  <a class="propellant-button propellant-button-secondary" href="/about">Learn more</a>
</div>
```

`propellant-section-angled` is a light section with the pale tint rising on an angle, and
`propellant-section-navy propellant-notch` is a Navy section with the notch below it. The full list
is in the [website spec](/web/websites/#the-propellant-stylesheet). For most content, the snippets
above are simpler: they work with normal Text and Button blocks, so anyone can edit the page later.

### Removing the code later

Open **Custom Code**, then **Custom CSS** (or **Code Injection**), select the lines from the
`/* Propellant website styles` comment down to the end of that snippet, delete them and click
**Save**. Your site goes back to the plain Site styles from Part 1. Keep the comment line on
anything you leave in place, so the next person knows where it came from.

## Check your work

On a computer:

- [ ] Every heading is in Oswald capitals. Paragraphs are in Lato, in sentence case.
- [ ] The eyebrow above the headline is small, light and widely spaced (if you added snippet A).
- [ ] Buttons are pills in Oswald capitals. On light sections the primary is solid Teal with White
      text; on dark sections buttons are Teal, or Cyan outlines if you added snippet B.
- [ ] Hovering a primary button on a light section clears it to a Teal outline (if you added
      snippet B).
- [ ] White, Warm White, Navy, Black and Deep Teal sections use Lightest 1, Light 1, Darkest 1,
      Darkest 2 and Dark 1, and dark and light sections alternate.
- [ ] Nothing on a dark section is Teal text. Text there is White, and links are Cyan.
- [ ] Photos and image blocks have square corners.
- [ ] The full color logo sits on a White or Warm White header, at least 24px tall, with room
      around it.
- [ ] The monogram shows in the browser tab.

On a phone (use the mobile view in the editor, then check the published site on a real phone):

- [ ] Heading 1 is about 40px and fits without breaking words awkwardly.
- [ ] The mobile logo is at least 24px tall.
- [ ] Buttons stay pill shaped and easy to tap.
- [ ] Sections have clear space above and below, about 64px.

Code can behave differently in the editor than on the live site. Open your published site in a
private window to see it the way visitors do.

## If something looks off

- **A heading is not in Oswald capitals.** Check the text is set to a heading in the format menu,
  not just made bigger, and that Site styles, **Fonts**, **Headings** is set to Oswald and
  Uppercase.
- **The eyebrow looks like a heavy heading.** Check snippet A is in the Custom CSS box and that
  you clicked Save. Then reload the page.
- **One block ignores the site colors or fonts.** Someone styled it with the text toolbar. Select
  the text and clear the formatting, or pick the format again from the format menu, so it follows
  Site styles.
- **A whole section changed color after you edited the palette.** Palette changes flow into the
  color themes. Open your five themes again and re-enter the values from the tables in Step 2.
- **Your fonts or buttons suddenly changed.** A theme or pack was clicked in Site styles. Use the
  undo arrow at the top of the panel, or set Step 1 or Step 3 again.
- **A button is square or stretched.** In a Fluid Engine section, set the Button block to **Fit**,
  not **Fill**. If all buttons are square, check **Shape** is **Pill** in Site styles, **Buttons**,
  for each button type.
- **The old browser icon still shows.** Browsers keep icons for a long time. Clear the cache or
  open the site in a private window.

# Webflow

Source: https://propellant.masschallenge.org/web/websites/webflow/

Webflow gives you everything you need to build a MassChallenge-style site without writing code.
You store the brand colors, fonts and sizes once as variables, style every heading, paragraph and
link at once, and make a handful of classes for buttons and sections. By the end you will have a
site with the right fonts, colors, Oswald headlines, pill buttons, dark Navy, Black and Deep Teal
sections alternating with White and Warm White ones, the logo and a site icon, and it will look
right on phones too. Plan on about two hours the first time,
most of it in Part 1.

Keep the [website spec](/web/websites/) open in another tab while you work. Every value in this
guide comes from it.

## Before you start

**Your plan.** You can do almost all of this guide on any Webflow plan, including the free one:

- Google Fonts, variables, tag styles and classes are part of the Designer (the Webflow editor).
  Webflow says you do not need a paid plan to use Google Fonts.
- Custom code (Part 4, optional) needs a paid Core, Growth, Agency or Freelancer Workspace, or an
  active Site plan on this site. You do not need custom code to follow the spec.
- Publishing to your own domain (such as yourdomain.org) needs a Site plan. Without one you can
  publish to a free `yoursite.webflow.io` address.

**Words you will meet.** Webflow uses a few terms from web design. Here is what they mean:

- **Variable**: a named, saved value, such as a color called Teal. Change it once and everything
  that uses it updates.
- **Tag style**: a style for every element of one kind, such as All H1 Headings. Webflow shows
  tags in pink.
- **Class**: a named style you give to chosen elements, such as a button. Webflow shows classes in
  blue.
- **Combo class**: a second class added after the first, which changes only a few things. A
  secondary button is the primary button class plus a combo class.
- **Breakpoint**: a screen width where your design can change, such as Mobile landscape.

**The logo files.** Download these from our public file store (right click each link, then save):

- Horizontal logo, full color, for White and Warm White backgrounds:
  [masschallenge-logo-horizontal-color.png](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/masschallenge/propellant-web@v2.0.0/assets/logos/masschallenge-logo-horizontal-color.png)
- Horizontal logo, white, for Navy, Black and Deep Teal backgrounds:
  [masschallenge-logo-horizontal-white.png](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/masschallenge/propellant-web@v2.0.0/assets/logos/masschallenge-logo-horizontal-white.png)
- Monogram, full color, for the site icon:
  [masschallenge-logo-monogram-color.png](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/masschallenge/propellant-web@v2.0.0/assets/logos/masschallenge-logo-monogram-color.png)

There are also `-black` versions of both lockups, and a `-white` monogram, at the same address. Use
these files only, never a copy of the logo from somewhere else. The
[brand guidelines](/brand/reference/) explain when to use each one.

## Part 1: Set up site styles (no code)

This is the heart of the guide. You will do it once, and every page you build afterwards starts
on brand.

### How Webflow styling works

Webflow styles in layers. The **Body (All Pages)** tag sets the defaults for the whole site. Tags
such as **All H1 Headings** and **All Paragraphs** then refine one kind of element. **Classes** sit
on top and change chosen elements, such as buttons and sections. Each layer only overrides what you
set on it, and everything else is inherited from the layer below.

**Variables** sit alongside this. You save each brand value once in the Variables panel and link
styles to it. You can then give a variable a second value for phones (a mode), so the mobile sizes
take care of themselves.

You do all of this in the **Style panel**, the panel on the right of the Designer. At the top of it
is the **Style selector** field, which shows what you are styling: a pink tag, a blue class or a
green state such as Hover.

### Step 1: Add Oswald

Lato is already built into the Webflow Designer, so you only need to add Oswald.

1. Open **Site settings**, then the **Fonts** tab.
2. Under **Google fonts**, choose **Oswald**.
3. Tick the **400** (Regular), **600** (SemiBold) and **700** (Bold) variants. Eyebrows use 400,
   headlines, subheads and buttons 600, and the big stat 700.
4. Click **Add font**.
5. Go back to the Designer and refresh the page in your browser. Oswald now appears in **Style
   panel > Typography > Font**, under Google fonts.

You will not see Lato in the Site settings list. That is expected: Webflow leaves out the Google
fonts it already includes. Lato is in the Font dropdown under Google fonts.

> Webflow notes that its Google Fonts connection sends visitors' IP addresses to Google. If your
> privacy rules do not allow that, download Lato and Oswald from Google Fonts and upload them under
> **Site settings > Fonts > Custom fonts** instead. Everything else in this guide stays the same.
