### Step 2: Make a Propellant variable collection

A collection keeps all the brand values together, so the next person can find them.

1. Open the **Variables** panel from the left toolbar of the Designer.
2. Click the **plus** icon next to **Site variables**.
3. Name the collection `Propellant` and click **Create**.

To add each variable below: click **New variable**, choose the type (Color, Size or Font Family),
then hover over the new variable's name and click the settings **cog** to rename it. Type the
name exactly as shown. The part before the slash puts it in a group, so `Colors/Teal` appears as
Teal inside a Colors group. Click the value to set it.

### Step 3: Add the color variables

Create one **Color** variable for each row. This is the spec palette.

| Variable name | Hex | Use it for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Colors/White` | `#FFFFFF` | Light section background, text on dark sections |
| `Colors/Warm White` | `#F8F8F5` | Alternate light section background |
| `Colors/Light tint` | `#F3FAFC` | The angled tint on a light section |
| `Colors/Navy` | `#10263F` | Dark section background |
| `Colors/Black` | `#222222` | Body text, and dark section background |
| `Colors/Deep Teal` | `#004F73` | Dark section background |
| `Colors/Teal` | `#00708E` | Headings, links and buttons on light |
| `Colors/Cyan` | `#54EEFF` | Text, links and outlines on dark sections only |
| `Colors/MC Blue` | `#0EABBC` | Graphic shapes only, never text |
| `Colors/Navy black` | `#051925` | The dark end of the hero overlay |
| `Colors/Ocean` | `#037AA6` | Gradient stop only, never a flat fill |
| `Colors/Slate` | `#4B575B` | Secondary text on light, such as captions |
| `Colors/Line` | `#DBE1E3` | Lines and dividers |
| `Colors/Yellow` | `#FFC801` | One warm accent: tags, rules and stats, with Black text |
| `Colors/Error` | `#BF0261` | Form errors only |

If your site already has swatches, Webflow has turned them into color variables. You can leave
them or delete the ones you no longer use.

### Step 4: Add the font variables

Create two **Font Family** variables:

| Variable name | Font |
| --- | --- |
| `Fonts/Body` | Lato |
| `Fonts/Headline` | Oswald |

### Step 5: Add the size variables

Create one **Size** variable for each row, using the **Desktop** value and the px unit. You will add
the Mobile values in the next step.

| Variable name | Desktop | Mobile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Type/Heading 1` | 64px | 40px |
| `Type/Heading 2` | 40px | 30px |
| `Type/Heading 3` | 30px | 24px |
| `Type/Heading 4` | 24px | 20px |
| `Type/Eyebrow` | 14px | 14px |
| `Type/Big stat` | 72px | 48px |
| `Type/Paragraph large` | 20px | 18px |
| `Type/Paragraph` | 17px | 16px |
| `Type/Paragraph small` | 14px | 14px |
| `Type/Button` | 16px | 16px |
| `Space/Section` | 96px | 64px |
| `Space/Button vertical` | 14px | 14px |
| `Space/Button horizontal` | 28px | 28px |
| `Layout/Text width` | 720px | 720px |
| `Radius/Pill` | 9999px | 9999px |

`Radius/Pill` is a very large corner radius, which is how a web page draws fully rounded pill
ends. Buttons are the only rounded thing on the site: cards and photos have square corners.
`Layout/Text width` keeps paragraphs to about 68 characters a line.

### Step 6: Add the mobile sizes with a mode

A mode is a second set of values for the same variables. A responsive mode switches on by itself at
a breakpoint, so you link each style once and it shrinks on phones automatically.

1. In the Variables panel, with the Propellant collection open, click the **New mode** dropdown
   arrow.
2. Name the mode `Mobile`.
3. In the **Responsive** dropdown, choose **Mobile landscape**. That covers screens 767px wide and
   below, which includes phones held either way.
4. Click **Create**. Every value starts as a copy of the Base (desktop) value.
5. In the Mobile column, click each value that changes and type the Mobile number from the table
   in Step 5: Heading 1 40px, Heading 2 30px, Heading 3 24px, Heading 4 20px, Big stat 48px,
   Paragraph large 18px, Paragraph 16px and Section 64px. Leave the others as they are.

You will check this on the Mobile portrait breakpoint in "Check your work".

### Step 7: Style the Body (All Pages) tag

These are the defaults every page inherits.

1. Open any page and click the **Body** element in the Navigator (the page structure list on the
   left).
2. In the Style panel, click the **Style selector** field. Under **HTML Tag**, choose **Body (All
   Pages)**.
3. Under **Typography**, set:
   - **Font**: hover over the field, click the purple dot in its top left corner and choose
     `Fonts/Body`. (This purple dot is how you link any field to a variable.)
   - **Weight**: 400 (Normal).
   - **Size**: link to `Type/Paragraph`.
   - **Height** (line height): type `1.5`, then choose the **-** unit so it has no unit. A unitless
     line height grows and shrinks with the text.
   - **Color**: link to `Colors/Black`.
4. Under **Backgrounds**, set **Color** to `Colors/White`.

Set the text color here, on the Body, and not on the paragraph tags. That way a dark section can
switch all its text to White in one place (Part 3).

### Step 8: Style All H1 to All H4 headings

Add a Heading to any page from **Add panel > Typography** so you have one to click. Select it, make
sure it has no class, then open the Style selector field and choose the tag. Set each tag as
below, and link the font and size to the variables shown.

| Tag | Font | Weight | Size | Height | Letter spacing | Letter case |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| All H1 Headings | `Fonts/Headline` | 600 (SemiBold) | `Type/Heading 1` | `1` (no unit) | `0` | All capitals |
| All H2 Headings | `Fonts/Headline` | 600 (SemiBold) | `Type/Heading 2` | `1` (no unit) | `0` | All capitals |
| All H3 Headings | `Fonts/Headline` | 600 (SemiBold) | `Type/Heading 3` | `1.1` (no unit) | `0` | All capitals |
| All H4 Headings | `Fonts/Headline` | 600 (SemiBold) | `Type/Heading 4` | `1.15` (no unit) | `0` | All capitals |

To change which heading level you are styling, select the heading and change its level (H1, H2
and so on) in the Settings panel, or add one heading of each level and select each in turn.

For every heading:

- **Letter spacing** and **letter case** are under **More type options** at the bottom of the
  Typography section. Choose the all capitals option (shown as **AA**) for letter case.
- Type headings in sentence case, such as "Founders build here". Webflow turns them into capitals
  for you. Screen readers then read words, not letters.
- If you cannot find the letter case control, use **Style panel > Custom properties** instead:
  click **Add**, type `text-transform` as the name and `uppercase` as the value, and press Enter.

Leave the color empty on All H1 Headings, so the headline inherits Black from the Body (or White
in a dark section). Set **Color** on All H2, All H3 and All H4 Headings to `Colors/Teal`. The dark
section classes in Step 12 turn them White.

### Step 9: Style All Paragraphs and All Links

**All Paragraphs.** Select a paragraph with no class, open the Style selector field and choose
**All Paragraphs**. Set:

- **Size**: link to `Type/Paragraph`.
- **Height**: `1.5` (no unit).
- **Size section > Max W** (maximum width): link to `Layout/Text width`.

**All Links.** Select a text link, open the Style selector field and choose **All Links**. Set:

- **Color**: link to `Colors/Teal`.
- **Decoration**: underline.

Webflow treats buttons as links too, so buttons start out teal and underlined. The button classes
in Step 11 fix that.

**Eyebrow, big stat and headline accent.** Make three more classes the same way:

| Class | On this element | Settings |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `eyebrow` | Paragraph above a headline | Font `Fonts/Headline`, Weight 400, Size `Type/Eyebrow`, Height `1.2`, Letter spacing `0.3em`, All capitals |
| `big-stat` | Paragraph or Heading holding a number | Font `Fonts/Headline`, Weight 700, Size `Type/Big stat`, Height `1`, Color `Colors/Teal` |
| `headline-accent` | A Span around the payoff words of a headline | Color `Colors/Teal` |

To make a span, double click the headline, select the payoff words and click the **+** (wrap in
span) button in the text toolbar.

### Step 10: Make the paragraph size classes

The spec has two more text sizes, so make a class for each. Select a paragraph, click the Style
selector field, type the class name and press Enter. Then set:

| Class | Size | Height | Color |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `paragraph-large` | `Type/Paragraph large` | `1.5` (no unit) | leave empty |
| `paragraph-small` | `Type/Paragraph small` | `1.5` (no unit) | `Colors/Slate` (for captions) |

### Step 11: Make the button classes

You will make one base class for the primary button, then two combo classes for the other button
styles. Webflow buttons come from **Add panel > Links > Button**.

**Primary button: `brand-button`.** Add a Button, click the Style selector field, type
`brand-button` and press Enter. Set:

- **Typography**: Font `Fonts/Headline`, Weight 600 (SemiBold), Size `Type/Button`, Height `1` (no
  unit), Letter spacing `0.05em`, All capitals, Color `Colors/White`, Decoration none (click the
  **X**).
- **Backgrounds**: Color `Colors/Teal`.
- **Spacing**: padding top and bottom `Space/Button vertical`, left and right
  `Space/Button horizontal`.
- **Borders**: Radius `Radius/Pill`, Border 2px solid `Colors/Teal`. No shadow.

Now the hover. Click the dropdown arrow in the Style selector field, choose **Hover** from the
**States** menu (a green Hover label appears), and set **Backgrounds > Color** to transparent and
**Typography > Color** to `Colors/Teal`, so the fill clears to a Teal outline. Choose **None** in
the same menu to go back to the normal state.

**Secondary button: `brand-button` plus `is-secondary`.** Add a second Button. Type
`brand-button`, press Enter, then type `is-secondary` and press Enter. The second class is a combo
class: it starts with everything from `brand-button` and only changes what you set here.

- **Backgrounds**: Color transparent.
- **Typography**: Color `Colors/Teal`.
- **Hover** state: Backgrounds Color `Colors/Teal`, Typography Color `Colors/White`.

**Button on a dark section: `brand-button` plus `is-on-dark`.** Add a third Button, apply
`brand-button`, then the combo class `is-on-dark`:

- **Backgrounds**: Color transparent.
- **Borders**: Color `Colors/Cyan`.
- **Typography**: Color `Colors/White`.
- **Hover** state: Backgrounds Color `Colors/Teal`, Borders Color `Colors/Teal`, Typography Color
  `Colors/White`.

Write button labels in sentence case with a verb, such as "Apply now" or "Meet the startups". The
capitals come from the class. For a "see all" link you can end the label with an arrow (→).

### Step 12: Make the section classes

Sections work the same way: one base class and combo classes for each color.

1. From **Add panel > Structure**, add a **Box**. (In older versions of Webflow, add a **Section**
   instead and skip the next step.)
2. In the **Settings** panel, set the **Tag** to **Section**.
3. Click the Style selector field, type `brand-section` and press Enter. Set:
   - **Spacing**: padding top and bottom `Space/Section`.
   - **Backgrounds**: Color `Colors/White`.
   - **Position**: Relative, so the notch below can sit on its edge.
4. Add sections with `brand-section` plus each combo class below:

| Combo class | Backgrounds | Typography color |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `is-warm-white` | Color `Colors/Warm White` | leave empty |
| `is-angled` | A **Linear gradient** at 174 degrees: `Colors/White` from 0% to 40%, then `Colors/Light tint` from 40% to 100% (two stops at the same place make a sharp edge) | leave empty |
| `is-navy` | Color `Colors/Navy` | `Colors/White` |
| `is-black` | Color `Colors/Black` | `Colors/White` |
| `is-deep-teal` | Color `Colors/Deep Teal` | `Colors/White` |

Headings H2 to H4 are Teal from Step 8, which is too dark for a dark section. Give any heading in a
dark section the class `heading-on-dark` with **Typography > Color** `Colors/White`. In the same
way, use `headline-accent` plus a combo class `is-on-dark`, and `big-stat` plus `is-on-dark`, with
**Typography > Color** `Colors/Cyan`.

**Links on dark sections.** Text links keep their Teal color, and Teal on Navy, Black or Deep Teal
is not allowed. Give any text link inside a dark section the class `link-on-dark` and set its
**Typography > Color** to `Colors/Cyan`.

**The notch.** Alternate dark and light sections down the page, and mark each change with a notch:
a small triangle that points down from one section into the next, in the color of the section
above it.

1. Inside a section, at the end, add a **Div Block** with the class `section-notch`.
2. Set **Position** to Absolute, **Top** 100%, **Left** 50%, **Size** 48px wide and 24px tall,
   **Z-index** 1, and **Transforms > Move** X to -50%.
3. Under **Custom properties**, add `clip-path` with the value `polygon(0 0, 100% 0, 50% 100%)`.
4. Set **Backgrounds > Color** to the section's color, with combo classes such as
   `section-notch is-navy`.

**White cards.** In a dark section, add a Div Block with the class `brand-card`: Backgrounds
`Colors/White`, Typography color `Colors/Black`, padding 24px, Radius 0. Inside it, an H3 for the
title and a paragraph. The title stays Teal from Step 8, so give it no extra class.

**Numbered blocks.** A Div Block with the class `numbered-block`: a 6px solid `Colors/Black` top
border and 16px of top padding. Inside it, a paragraph with the class `numbered-number` (Font
`Fonts/Headline`, Weight 600, Size `Type/Heading 2`, Color `Colors/Teal`), an H3 for the title and
a paragraph.

**Hero with a photo.** A `brand-section is-navy` with two background layers: under **Backgrounds**,
add an **Image** layer with your photo (chosen by the [images guide](/guidelines/images/#brand-photography))
set to Cover, then add a **Linear gradient** layer above it, at 90 degrees, from `Colors/Navy black`
at 30% opacity on the text side to `Colors/Ocean` at 15% opacity on the subject side. Warm light
should still glow through; if warm areas turn gray or blue, lower the opacity.

### Step 13: Square images and cards

Select an image, open the Style selector field and choose **All Images**. Set **Borders > Radius**
to 0. Keep the radius at 0 on any card class you make later. Only buttons are rounded.

### Step 14 (only if needed): Mobile without modes

The Mobile mode in Step 6 should handle phone sizes everywhere. If a size does not change on a
phone, set it directly: click the **Mobile landscape** icon in the canvas bar (above the canvas),
select the element, choose the same tag or class in the Style selector, and type the Mobile value
from the table in Step 5. Styles set on Mobile landscape also apply to Mobile portrait.

## Part 2: Add the logo and site icon

### The logo

In Webflow the logo is part of the page, in the navigation bar, rather than a site setting.

1. Open the **Assets** panel in the left toolbar, click the **cloud** icon and upload the
   horizontal color logo (and the white one, for dark sections and the footer).
2. From **Add panel > Other**, drag a **Navbar** to the top of your page.
3. Drag the color logo from the Assets panel into the Navbar's **Brand** link.
4. Select the logo image and set **Style panel > Size > Height** to `32px`, with width left on
   Auto so the proportions stay right. Never go below 24px tall (160px wide); on very small spaces
   use the monogram instead.
5. In the image's settings, set the alt text (the description screen readers announce) to
   `MassChallenge`.
6. Select the Brand link, open **Settings panel > Link settings**, choose **Page** and pick your
   home page.

Keep clear space around the logo equal to the height of the "M" in the MASSCHALLENGE wordmark, on
every side, and align it to a corner or the top edge of its area. Do not stretch, recolor or add
effects. On a Navy, Black or Deep Teal background, use the white logo.

To make the Navbar appear on every page, right click it and turn it into a component, then add that
component to each page.

### The site icon (favicon)

The site icon is the little picture in the browser tab. Webflow needs one square image and makes
every size from it.

1. Make the monogram square first. The monogram file is wider than it is tall, so open it in any
   image editor, put it in the middle of a square transparent canvas, and add empty space above
   and below. Do not stretch or crop it.
2. Open **Site settings > General > Icons** and click **Upload icon**.
3. Upload your square monogram and select which icons to update.
4. Click **Apply**, then publish your site and refresh it in your browser to see the new icon.

## Part 3: Build on brand pages

With Part 1 done, building a page is mostly a matter of choosing the right class. The quickest way
to apply a class is to select an element, click the Style selector field (or press Command + Enter
on a Mac, Control + Enter on Windows), start typing the name and press Enter.

| You want | Element | Classes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A White section | Box with the Section tag | `brand-section` |
| A Warm White section | Box with the Section tag | `brand-section` `is-warm-white` |
| A light section with the angled tint | Box with the Section tag | `brand-section` `is-angled` |
| A Navy, Black or Deep Teal section | Box with the Section tag | `brand-section` `is-navy`, `is-black` or `is-deep-teal` |
| The notch below a section | Div Block | `section-notch` and the section's color |
| The eyebrow | Paragraph | `eyebrow` |
| The headline | Heading set to H1 | none (the tag does it) |
| The payoff of a two toned headline | Span | `headline-accent` |
| A big number | Paragraph | `big-stat` |
| A white card | Div Block | `brand-card` |
| A numbered block | Div Block | `numbered-block` |
| A primary button | Button | `brand-button` |
| A secondary button | Button | `brand-button` `is-secondary` |
| A button on a dark section | Button | `brand-button` `is-on-dark` |
| A heading on a dark section | Heading | `heading-on-dark` |
| A link on a dark section | Text link | `link-on-dark` |
| An intro paragraph | Paragraph | `paragraph-large` |
| A caption or note | Paragraph | `paragraph-small` |

To apply a combo class, apply the base class first, then type the combo class name. Typing a
comma after the first name adds it and lets you type the next one straight away.

A few rules from the spec to keep in mind:

- Use one H1 per page, for the headline. Use H2, H3 and H4 for everything below it.
- Never put Teal text or a solid primary button on a dark section. Use White text, Cyan accents and
  the `is-on-dark` button.
- Use one warm accent per page, such as a Yellow tag or rule, always with Black text on Yellow.
- Put text over a photo only on a calm, high contrast area. Otherwise move it, or set it on a solid
  Navy, Black or Deep Teal block.

### Build a sample home page

1. Add the Navbar component with the logo at the top.
2. **Hero, on Navy with a photo.** Add the hero section. Inside it, add an `eyebrow`, a Heading set
   to H1 (for example "Founders build here") with a `headline-accent` span on the payoff, a
   paragraph with `paragraph-large`, and a `brand-button` `is-on-dark` ("Apply now"). Add a
   `section-notch is-navy` at the end.
3. **How it works, on White with the angled tint.** Add a `brand-section` `is-angled` with an H2 and
   three `numbered-block` Div Blocks, then a `brand-button` ("Learn more").
4. **Highlights, on Navy.** Add a `brand-section` `is-navy` with an H2 and three `brand-card` Div
   Blocks, then a `section-notch is-navy`.
5. **Footer, on Black.** Add a `brand-section` `is-black` with the white logo and your links, each
   with `link-on-dark`.
6. Click **Preview** (the eye icon) to see the page as a visitor would, then switch to the Mobile
   landscape and Mobile portrait breakpoints in the canvas bar to check phones.

### Publish

1. Click **Publish** at the top right of the Designer (or press Shift + P).
2. Tick the domain(s) to publish to: your `webflow.io` address, your own domain, or both.
3. Click **Publish to selected domains**.

To try changes before they go public, tick only the `webflow.io` address.

## Part 4: Custom code (optional)

**You do not need custom code for Webflow.** Parts 1 to 3 cover the whole spec with Webflow's own
variables, tags and classes, and those are the better choice: the next person can see and change
them in the Style panel, and they show on the canvas while you edit. If you ever need a style that
the Style panel has no control for, add it under **Style panel > Custom properties** on the class
or tag. That is still no code to maintain.

### Alternative: the Propellant stylesheet

If you would rather use our ready made classes than build your own, you can load the Propellant
stylesheet and type its class names into Webflow. Use this instead of Steps 10 to 12 of Part 1, not
as well as them. You still need Step 1 (Oswald), and the tag styles from Steps 7 to 9 are still
worth doing.

This needs a paid Core, Growth, Agency or Freelancer Workspace, or an active Site plan.

1. Open **Site settings**, then the **Custom code** tab.
2. Paste this into the **Head code** box:

   ```html
   <!-- Propellant website styles: see github.com/masschallenge/propellant-web -->
   <link
     rel="stylesheet"
     href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/masschallenge/propellant-web@v2.0.0/dist/website.css"
   />
   ```

   The first line is a label, so the next person knows where the code came from. Keep it.

3. Click **Save changes**, then publish.
4. In the Designer, select an element, click the Style selector field, type one of the class names
   below and press Enter. Do not add any styles to these classes in the Style panel; the
   stylesheet does that.

| On this element | Type this class | What you get |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Heading set to H1 | `propellant-headline` | The Oswald capitals headline |
| Paragraph | `propellant-eyebrow` | The tracked eyebrow |
| Button | `propellant-button` | The primary pill button |
| Button | `propellant-button`, then `propellant-button-secondary` | The secondary button |
| Box with the Section tag | `propellant-section-navy`, `propellant-section-black` or `propellant-section-deep-teal` | A dark section with White text, Cyan links and Cyan outline buttons |
| Box with the Section tag | `propellant-section-warm-white` or `propellant-section-angled` | A light section |
| Box with the Section tag | `propellant-notch`, as well as a section class | The notch below the section |
| Div Block | `propellant-card` | A white card with square corners |
| Text link | `propellant-link` | An underlined link: Teal on light, Cyan on dark |
| Paragraph | `propellant-body` | Paragraph text |
| Paragraph | `propellant-caption` | Small print, such as dates and notes |
| Section or Box | `propellant-text` | The body font and text color for a whole section |

Things to know:

- The stylesheet's styles appear in **Preview** and on the published site, but you may not see
  them on the canvas while you edit. That is why Webflow's own classes are easier to work with.
- The stylesheet uses the same values as the spec and loads Lato and Oswald itself. Keep Oswald
  in Site settings > Fonts anyway, so it also shows on the canvas while you edit.

**To remove it later:** take the `propellant-` classes off your elements (click the class in the
Style selector and press Delete), delete the lines from **Site settings > Custom code > Head
code**, click **Save changes** and publish again.

## Check your work

On desktop, in Preview and on the published site:

- [ ] The H1 headline is Oswald SemiBold, in capitals, 64px, and there is only one per page.
- [ ] All headings are Oswald capitals, and all body text is Lato, in sentence case, in Black.
- [ ] Links are Teal and underlined on light sections, and Cyan on dark ones.
- [ ] Primary buttons are Teal pills in Oswald capitals with White text, and clear to a Teal
      outline on hover.
- [ ] Secondary buttons are Teal outlines that fill with Teal on hover.
- [ ] Dark sections have White text, Cyan outline buttons and the white logo, and no Teal text.
- [ ] Dark and light sections alternate, with a notch where they meet.
- [ ] Cards and images have square corners.
- [ ] Sections have about 96px of space above and below, and paragraphs stop at about 720px wide.
- [ ] The logo is the official file, at least 24px tall, and links to the home page.
- [ ] The site icon shows the monogram in the browser tab.

On a phone (or the Mobile landscape and Mobile portrait breakpoints):

- [ ] The H1 is 40px, H2 30px, H3 24px, H4 20px and paragraphs 16px.
- [ ] Sections have about 64px of space above and below.
- [ ] Buttons stay pills and their labels fit on one line.

## If something looks off

- **Headings are still in Webflow's default font or size.** The heading probably has a class with
  its own font or size. Select it, look at the Style selector, and remove the class (or reset the
  font and size on it) so it falls back to the All H1 to All H4 tags.
- **Text in a dark section is dark.** The color was set on a paragraph tag or class rather than on
  the Body, or a heading has no nested White color for that section. Clear the color there (click the blue or pink label next to Color and
  choose Reset) so it inherits White from the section.
- **Buttons are underlined or turn a different color on hover.** Buttons inherit from All Links.
  Select the button, set **Decoration** to none on `brand-button`, and check that the Hover state
  is set on the button class, not only on All Links.
- **Sizes do not shrink on phones.** Check that the Mobile mode in the Variables panel has its
  Responsive setting on Mobile landscape, and that the style is linked to a variable (the value
  shows in purple). If it shows a plain number, link it to the variable, or use Step 14.
- **Oswald is missing from the Font list.** Refresh the Designer after adding it in Site settings.
  If it is still missing, check that it is listed under **Site settings > Fonts > Google fonts**.
- **The stylesheet classes do nothing.** Custom code only runs in Preview and on the published
  site, and only after you save it and publish. Check that the code is in Head code, not Footer
  code, and that your plan includes custom code.

# Wix

Source: https://propellant.masschallenge.org/web/websites/wix/

This guide gives a Wix site the MassChallenge look: Oswald headlines in capitals, Lato text, the
brand palette, pill shaped Oswald buttons, dark and light sections and the right logo in the
header. It covers both of Wix's editors, the Wix Editor
and Wix Studio, and says clearly where they differ. Setting up the styles takes about an hour. Plan
on another hour if you are building a home page from scratch.

Wix has more than one editor, and each puts the style settings in a different place. Check which
one you have before you start:

- **Wix Editor** (the classic editor): the left side of the screen has a **Site Design** button
  (called Theme Manager in some older versions).
- **Wix Studio**: the left side of the screen has a **Site Styles** button.
- If you see a **Brand** button at the top of the editor instead, your site uses Wix's newer
  editor (Wix Harmony). The values in this guide still apply: enter them under **Brand**, then
  **Colors**, **Text** and **Buttons**.

## Before you start

**Plans.** You can do almost everything in this guide on any Wix plan, free included. A few steps
need more:

| Step | Wix Editor | Wix Studio |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Site styles, logo, sections and buttons (Parts 1 to 3) | Any plan | Any plan |
| Site icon (favicon, the small picture in the browser tab) | Paid (Premium) plan, a connected domain and a published site | Same as Wix Editor |
| CSS editing in `global.css` (Part 4) | Usually not available (see Part 4) | Available in the editor's Code panel. Wix's help pages list no plan requirement |
| Custom code in the page head (Part 5) | Published site with a connected domain, which needs a paid plan | Same as Wix Editor |

A connected domain means your own web address, such as `yourname.org`, instead of a free
`wixsite.com` address. Wix only lets you connect one on a paid plan.

**Keep the spec open.** Every value in this guide comes from the
[website spec](/web/websites/). Open it in a second browser tab so you can copy hex codes (the six
character color codes that start with `#`) straight from it.

**Download the logo files.** Use only the official files. Save these to your computer:

- [masschallenge-logo-horizontal-color.png](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/masschallenge/propellant-web@v2.0.0/assets/logos/masschallenge-logo-horizontal-color.png),
  for white and light backgrounds.
- [masschallenge-logo-horizontal-white.png](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/masschallenge/propellant-web@v2.0.0/assets/logos/masschallenge-logo-horizontal-white.png),
  for Navy, Black and Deep Teal sections and dark photos.
- [masschallenge-logo-monogram-color.png](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/masschallenge/propellant-web@v2.0.0/assets/logos/masschallenge-logo-monogram-color.png),
  for the site icon.

There are also `-black` versions of both lockups (for example
`masschallenge-logo-horizontal-black.png`) at the same address, for places where only one dark
color works. Read the [logo rules](/brand/reference/#logo) once before you place the logo: never
stretch, recolor or crop it.

## Part 1: Set up site styles (no code)

This is where most of the work happens. Set the styles once and every themed element on the site
picks them up. Follow the section for your editor.

### Wix Editor

The Wix Editor has three site-wide settings: a **color theme**, a **text theme** (named text
styles: Heading 1 to Heading 6 and Paragraph 1 to Paragraph 3) and the colors for **primary and
secondary buttons**. Button shape and padding are set on a button itself, then copied.

#### Step 1: Set the theme colors

The color theme has two kinds of color. **Base colors** run from light to dark: Wix uses the
lightest for backgrounds and the darkest for text, and builds a range of shades between them.
**Accent colors** are used for links, buttons and menus.

1. In the editor, click **Site Design** on the left.
2. Click **Color theme**. In some versions you hover over **Color & Text Theme** and click
   **Customize** instead.
3. Click a color in the panel, type its hex code into the HEX field, and click **Apply**. Set them
   from this table:

   | Wix slot | Spec color | Hex |
   | --- | --- | --- |
   | Base color, lightest (backgrounds) | White | `#FFFFFF` |
   | Base color, darkest (text) | Black | `#222222` |
   | Accent color 1 | Teal | `#00708E` |
   | Accent color 2 | Navy | `#10263F` |
   | Accent color 3 | Deep Teal | `#004F73` |
   | Accent color 4 | Cyan | `#54EEFF` |

   If your panel shows fewer accent slots, fill them in this order and stop when you run out.
   If it shows more, use Warm White `#F8F8F5` and Slate `#4B575B` next.

4. Open **Advanced Settings** (at the bottom of the color panel). Click the color box next to each
   item and set:

   | Group | Item | Spec color | Hex |
   | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   | General | Primary background | White | `#FFFFFF` |
   | General | Secondary background | Warm White | `#F8F8F5` |
   | General | Lines and dividers | Line | `#DBE1E3` |
   | Text | Titles | Teal | `#00708E` |
   | Text | Paragraphs | Black | `#222222` |
   | Text | Subtitles | Slate | `#4B575B` |
   | Text | Links | Teal | `#00708E` |
   | Buttons | Primary, regular | Teal | `#00708E` |
   | Buttons | Primary, hover | White | `#FFFFFF` |
   | Buttons | Secondary, regular | White | `#FFFFFF` |
   | Buttons | Secondary, hover | Teal | `#00708E` |
   | Buttons | Disabled | Line | `#DBE1E3` |

   The exact item names in this panel vary between sites. Match each item to the closest row.
   If the panel also asks for button text colors, use White `#FFFFFF` on primary buttons and Teal
   `#00708E` on their hover, and Teal on secondary buttons with White on their hover. Step 4 adds
   the Teal outline that holds both together.

5. Save the remaining spec colors so they are one click away later: Warm White `#F8F8F5`, Black
   `#222222`, Light tint `#F3FAFC`, Slate `#4B575B`, Line `#DBE1E3`, Yellow `#FFC801` and Error
   `#BF0261`. In any color picker, use **My colors** and the add option (a plus sign) to save each
   one.

Only use Cyan on Navy, Black and Deep Teal sections, and never put Teal text on them. Use one warm
accent per page, such as Yellow behind Black text on a tag. The error color is for form error
messages, never decoration. MC Blue `#0EABBC` is for the logo and graphic shapes, never text.

#### Step 2: Check that Lato and Oswald are in your font list

1. Select any text box on the page and click **Edit Text**.
2. Open the **Fonts** drop-down and look for **Lato** and **Oswald**. Wix lists font weights as
   separate entries in some cases, so you may see **Oswald SemiBold** or **Oswald Light** listed on
   their own. You want Oswald SemiBold for headings and buttons and Oswald Regular for eyebrows.
3. If either font is missing, upload it:
   1. Download the font from Google Fonts ([Lato](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Lato) and
      [Oswald](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Oswald)). You need Lato Regular, Lato Bold, Oswald
      Regular, Oswald SemiBold and Oswald Bold.
   2. In the same **Fonts** drop-down, click **Upload Fonts** and choose the file (TTF, OTF, WOFF
      or WOFF2 all work).
   3. Click **Done** when it finishes. Uploaded fonts appear under **My Fonts** in the drop-down.

Uploaded fonts do not work in the Wix Blog and some Wix apps, so prefer the built-in Lato and
Oswald when they are listed.

#### Step 3: Set the text theme

1. Click **Site Design**, then **Text theme**.
2. Set **Heading Font** to **Oswald** and **Paragraph Font** to **Lato**.
3. Click **Customize heading styles**. Hover over each style, click the edit (pencil) icon, and
   enter the values from the table below. Then do the same under **Customize paragraph styles**.

| Wix style | Spec style | Font | Bold | Size | Line spacing | Character spacing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Heading 1 | Heading 1 (the headline) | Oswald SemiBold | Off | 64px | 1.0 | 0 |
| Heading 2 | Heading 2 | Oswald SemiBold | Off | 40px | 1.0 | 0 |
| Heading 3 | Heading 3 (subhead) | Oswald SemiBold | Off | 30px | 1.1 | 0 |
| Heading 4 | Heading 4 | Oswald SemiBold | Off | 24px | 1.15 | 0 |
| Heading 5 | Eyebrow | Oswald (Regular) | Off | 14px | 1.2 | 0.3em (30%) |
| Heading 6 | Big stat | Oswald | On | 72px | 1.0 | 0 |
| Paragraph 1 | Paragraph large | Lato | Off | 20px | 1.5 | 0 |
| Paragraph 2 | Paragraph | Lato | Off | 17px | 1.5 | 0 |
| Paragraph 3 | Paragraph small | Lato | Off | 14px | 1.5 | 0 |

Notes on the fields:

- **Line spacing.** Wix may show this as a number (enter the value above) or in pixels. For pixels,
  multiply the size by the line spacing: 64px for Heading 1, 40px for Heading 2, 33px for Heading
  3, 28px for Heading 4, 17px for Heading 5, 72px for Heading 6, 30px for Paragraph 1, 26px for
  Paragraph 2 and 21px for Paragraph 3.
- **Character spacing.** Only the eyebrow has any. If the field takes a small decimal, enter
  `0.3`. If it takes a percentage, enter `30`.
- **Color.** Set Heading 1 and the paragraphs to Black `#222222`, and Headings 2 to 4 and the big
  stat to Teal `#00708E`. In dark sections you change them to White (Part 3).
- **Heading 5 and 6** become the eyebrow and the big stat, because Wix has no other named styles
  for them. Use Heading 5 only for eyebrows and Heading 6 only for large numbers.
- **Capitals.** The Wix Editor has no setting that turns a style into capitals. Type headings,
  eyebrows and button labels in capitals, for example BUILT FOR THE WORLD. Type paragraphs in
  sentence case, never in capitals.

Any change to a style updates all the text on the site that already uses it.

#### Step 4: Design one primary button and one secondary button

The Wix Editor has no site-wide button shape setting, so you style one button and reuse it.

1. Click **Add Elements** on the left, then **Button**, and add a **Themed** button so it picks up
   your theme colors.
2. Select the button, click the **Design** icon, then **Customize Design**.
3. Set the **Regular** state:
   - **Fill:** Teal `#00708E`, opacity 100%.
   - **Borders:** width 2px, Teal `#00708E`.
   - **Corners:** click the lock so all four corners change together, then enter `100`. Any number
     at least half the button's height makes the fully rounded pill ends. Never use square
     corners: square cornered buttons are retired.
   - **Shadows:** off.
   - **Text:** Oswald SemiBold, 16px, White `#FFFFFF`, character spacing 0.05em (5%).
   - **Layout:** padding of about 14px above and below the text and 28px on each side. If your
     button only offers side padding, set 28px there and make the button about 44px tall.
4. Switch to the **Hover** state and set **Fill** to opacity 0% (or White on a White section) and
   the text to Teal `#00708E`, keeping the Teal border. The fill clears to a Teal outline.
5. Type a label in capitals with a verb, such as APPLY NOW.
6. For a **secondary** button, duplicate the primary button (copy and paste it) and swap the
   states: Regular fill opacity 0%, text Teal; Hover fill Teal, text White.
7. Keep these two buttons on a spare page or in a hidden spot. Copy and paste them whenever you
   need a new button, so every button stays the same.

#### Step 5: Set the mobile sizes

The Wix Editor has a separate mobile editor. Changes you make there only affect phones. Text you
added on desktop keeps its wording, but you can change its size on mobile.

1. Click the phone icon at the top of the editor to switch to the mobile view.
2. Select each heading and paragraph and set its size to the mobile value:

| Style | Mobile size |
| --- | --- |
| Heading 1 | 40px |
| Heading 2 | 30px |
| Heading 3 | 24px |
| Heading 4 | 20px |
| Big stat (Heading 6) | 48px |
| Paragraph large (Paragraph 1) | 18px |
| Paragraph (Paragraph 2) | 16px |
| Paragraph small (Paragraph 3) | 14px |
| Button text | 16px |

3. Check that buttons stay pill shaped and that sections have about 64px of space above and below
   their content.

### Wix Studio

Wix Studio keeps colors and text styles in one panel called **Site Styles**. It has no site-wide
button style yet, so buttons are styled one at a time or, better, with the short CSS in Part 4.

#### Step 1: Set the site colors

Every Studio site has at least six numbered colors, each tied to a job across the site and its
apps. You can add more, up to 25.

1. Click **Site Styles** on the left side of the editor, then the **Colors** tab.
2. Click a color, type the hex code into the HEX field, and click **Apply**. Set them from this
   table:

   | Studio color | What Wix uses it for | Spec color | Hex |
   | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   | Color 1 | Primary background | White | `#FFFFFF` |
   | Color 2 | Secondary background | Warm White | `#F8F8F5` |
   | Color 3 | Disabled items | Line | `#DBE1E3` |
   | Color 4 | Secondary text | Slate | `#4B575B` |
   | Color 5 | Primary text | Black | `#222222` |
   | Color 6 | Links and actions | Teal | `#00708E` |

   Your template may give these colors names, such as Primary background. Go by the job, not the
   name.

3. Add the rest of the spec palette as extra site colors, and rename each one to its spec name
   (hover over a color, click the **More Actions** icon, then **Rename**):

   | Name | Hex |
   | --- | --- |
   | Navy | `#10263F` |
   | Deep Teal | `#004F73` |
   | Cyan | `#54EEFF` |
   | Light tint | `#F3FAFC` |
   | MC Blue | `#0EABBC` |
   | Yellow | `#FFC801` |
   | Error | `#BF0261` |

#### Step 2: Set the fonts

1. In **Site Styles**, open the **Typography** tab.
2. Under **Fonts**, set the heading font to **Oswald** and the paragraph font to **Lato**, and click
   **Update**.
3. If Lato or Oswald is missing from the list, upload it:
   1. Download it from Google Fonts ([Lato](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Lato) and
      [Oswald](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Oswald)).
   2. Select any text element, click the **Open Inspector** icon at the top right, scroll to
      **Design** and open the **Font** drop-down.
   3. Click **Upload fonts** at the bottom, then **Upload Fonts**, and choose the file (TTF, OTF,
      WOFF or WOFF2). Click **Close** when it is done. It now appears under **Uploaded fonts**.

#### Step 3: Set the text styles

Studio has nine text styles: Heading 1 to Heading 6 (H1 to H6) and Paragraph 1 to Paragraph 3.
Each one has a **scale** option that sets a largest and smallest size, so the text shrinks
smoothly on small screens. That is how you set the mobile sizes.

1. In **Site Styles**, **Typography**, under **Text styles**, click a style.
2. Set the font, weight, size, line spacing, character spacing and color from the table below.
3. Turn on **scale** and enter the largest size as the maximum and the mobile size as the minimum.
4. Click the arrow at the top left to go back, and do the next style.

| Studio style | Spec style | Font and weight | Max size | Min size | Line spacing | Character spacing | Color |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Heading 1 | Heading 1 (the headline) | Oswald, SemiBold (600) | 64px | 40px | 1.0 | 0 | Black |
| Heading 2 | Heading 2 | Oswald, SemiBold (600) | 40px | 30px | 1.0 | 0 | Teal |
| Heading 3 | Heading 3 (subhead) | Oswald, SemiBold (600) | 30px | 24px | 1.1 | 0 | Teal |
| Heading 4 | Heading 4 | Oswald, SemiBold (600) | 24px | 20px | 1.15 | 0 | Teal |
| Heading 5 | Eyebrow | Oswald, Regular (400) | 14px | 14px | 1.2 | 0.3em (30%) | Black |
| Heading 6 | Big stat | Oswald, Bold (700) | 72px | 48px | 1.0 | 0 | Teal |
| Paragraph 1 | Paragraph large | Lato, Regular (400) | 20px | 18px | 1.5 | 0 | Black |
| Paragraph 2 | Paragraph | Lato, Regular (400) | 17px | 16px | 1.5 | 0 | Black |
| Paragraph 3 | Paragraph small | Lato, Regular (400) | 14px | 14px | 1.5 | 0 | Black |

If the style panel only offers a **Bold** switch rather than a weight list, pick **Oswald
SemiBold** from the font list for the headings if it is there (uploaded or built in), and turn Bold
off. If line spacing is in pixels, use the pixel values from the Wix Editor notes above. Studio,
like the Wix Editor, has no capitals setting in Site Styles: type headings, eyebrows and button
labels in capitals, or add the short CSS in Part 4 so Wix does it for you.

#### Step 4: Style your buttons

Site Styles does not include buttons yet (Wix lists it as a feature request). You have two
options:

- **Recommended: use the button CSS in Part 4.** It styles every button on the site in one go and
  keeps them consistent.
- **Without code:** select a button, click **Open Inspector**, and under **Design** set the same
  values as the Wix Editor button in Step 4 above: Teal fill, a 2px Teal border, White Oswald
  SemiBold 16px text in capitals, no shadow, corners of `100`, padding of about 14px by 28px, and a
  hover that clears the fill to a Teal outline with Teal text. Then copy and paste that button
  wherever you need one.

#### Step 5: Check the mobile breakpoint

Studio shows a desktop, tablet and mobile view at the top of the editor. These are breakpoints:
the screen widths where the layout can change.

1. Click the mobile view.
2. Check that the text has shrunk to the minimum sizes you set.
3. Select each section and set about 64px of space above and below its content (96px on
   desktop).

## Part 2: Add the logo and site icon

### The logo in the header

The steps are close to identical in both editors.

1. Click the header at the top of any page, so you edit the header shared by every page.
2. Add an image: in the Wix Editor, click **Add Elements**, then **Image**. In Wix Studio, use the
   add panel on the left. Upload `masschallenge-logo-horizontal-color.png`.
3. Place it at the left of the header, lined up with the content below it.
4. Resize it by dragging a corner, never a side, so it keeps its shape. Keep it at least 24px tall
   (160px wide). About 32px tall is a good header size.
5. Leave clear space around it equal to the height of the "M" in the MASSCHALLENGE wordmark, on
   every side. No text, edge or other image inside that space. Align it to a corner or the top
   edge of the header.
6. Link it to the home page: select the logo, click the link icon, choose **Page**, then **Home**.
7. Give it alt text (the description screen readers read out) of `MassChallenge`. In the Wix
   Editor this is in the image **Settings**. In Studio it is in the **Inspector**.

If your header is Navy, Black, Deep Teal or a dark photo, use
`masschallenge-logo-horizontal-white.png` instead. Never place the full color logo on a dark color.

### The site icon (favicon)

The site icon needs a paid plan, a connected domain and a published site. Wix needs a square image
whose sides are a multiple of 48px. The monogram file is wider than it is tall, so make a square
version first:

1. In any image editor, make a new square canvas of 192 by 192 pixels with a transparent
   background.
2. Place `masschallenge-logo-monogram-color.png` in the middle, scaled down so it does not touch
   the edges. Do not stretch it.
3. Export it as a PNG.

Then upload it:

1. Go to your site's dashboard and click **Settings**.
2. Click **Website settings**.
3. Under **Favicon**, click **Upload Image**, choose your PNG, and save.

Search engines decide whether and when to show the new icon in results, so it may take a while to
appear there.

## Part 3: Build on brand pages

A MassChallenge page alternates dark sections (Navy, Black or Deep Teal) with light ones (White or
Warm White). Stack them so neighboring sections differ: dark, then light, then dark.

### Make the sections

**White section:**

- **Wix Editor:** right-click the section (or click a strip) and choose **Change Background**.
  Under **Color**, pick White `#FFFFFF`.
- **Wix Studio:** select the section, click **Open Inspector**, click the color box under
  **Design** and pick Color 1 (White).

**Warm White section:**

- The same steps, with Warm White `#F8F8F5`. In Studio it is Color 2.

**Light section with an angled edge** (Wix Studio):

- Set the background to a **Gradient** in the same color box: a linear gradient at 174 degrees,
  White `#FFFFFF` up to 40% and Light tint `#F3FAFC` from 40%. Put the two stops at the same point,
  so the edge is sharp. Use a Teal headline and a Teal primary button in it.

**Navy, Black or Deep Teal section:**

1. Set the background to Navy `#10263F`, Black `#222222` or Deep Teal `#004F73` the same way.
2. Set every heading and paragraph in it to White `#FFFFFF`: select the text and change its color.
3. Use Cyan `#54EEFF` for accents and links, such as the payoff of a two toned headline. Never put
   Teal `#00708E` text on a dark section.
4. Use the white logo if the logo appears here.
5. Style the buttons as described in "Buttons on dark sections" below.

**The notch.** Mark the change from one section to the next with a small triangle that points down
from the section above, centered on the edge, in that section's color. Add a **Shape** (a triangle
pointing down) from **Add Elements**, color it to match the section above, about 48px wide and
24px tall, and place it centered on the edge between the two sections. Attach it to the section
above so it moves with it.

**White cards.** On a dark section, add a **Container** (Wix Editor: a **Box**) with a White fill,
square corners (0) and a Teal Heading 3 title and a Black paragraph inside.

**Numbered blocks.** A Container with a 6px Black top border only, then a number such as 01 in
Heading 2 (Teal), a Heading 3 title and a Paragraph 2.

**Hero with a photo.** Set the section background to an image chosen by the
[images guide](/guidelines/images/#brand-photography), then add the overlay: in the background settings,
turn on **Overlay** (or **Color overlay**) and choose a gradient from Navy black `#051925` on the
text side to Ocean `#037AA6` on the subject side, at 15 to 30% opacity. Warm light should still
glow through. Put text only on a calm area of the photo; otherwise set it on a solid Navy, Black or
Deep Teal Container.

In Studio, a section's background can differ by breakpoint. Check the mobile view to make sure it
stayed the same.

### Section spacing and width

- Give each section about 96px of empty space above and below its content on desktop and 64px on
  mobile.
- Make paragraph text boxes about 720px wide, so lines run to roughly 68 characters. Drag the side
  of the text box, or set the width in Studio's Inspector.
- Keep images and cards square cornered: select the image, open its design settings, and set
  **Corners** to 0. Only buttons are rounded.
- Leave generous margins. When in doubt, add space.

### Add the eyebrow and the headline

1. Add a text box with the **Heading 5** style for the eyebrow, a few words in capitals above the
   headline.
2. Add a text box and choose the **Heading 1** style from the text style drop-down (in the Wix
   Editor, click **Edit Text**, then the **Styles** drop-down).
3. Type the headline in capitals, unless you added the CSS from Part 4 in Studio, in which case
   type it in sentence case.
4. For a two toned headline, select the payoff words and color them Teal `#00708E` on light
   sections or Cyan `#54EEFF` on dark ones.
5. Use one Heading 1 per page, at the top. Use Heading 2 and Heading 3 for everything below it,
   in order: it helps search engines and people using screen readers.

### Add primary and secondary buttons

- Copy and paste your saved primary button for the main action on a section, such as Apply now.
- Use the secondary button (a Teal outline) for the second action next to it, such as Learn more.
- Give each section one primary button at most.
- Write labels in capitals, starting with a verb (in sentence case if you added the Part 4 CSS).
  For a "see all" link you can end the label with an arrow (→).

### Buttons on dark sections

A solid Teal button is too dark for a dark section, so buttons there are outlines:

- **Regular:** fill opacity 0%, a 2px Cyan `#54EEFF` border, text White `#FFFFFF`.
- **Hover:** fill Teal `#00708E`, border Teal, text White.
- Same pill shape and padding as the other buttons.

Style one, then copy it for every dark section. In Studio, the Part 4 CSS does this for you.

### Build a sample home page

1. **Opening (Navy, with a photo and the hero overlay):** an eyebrow, a Heading 1 headline, one
   Paragraph 1 line under it, and a Cyan outline button. A Navy notch below it.
2. **What you offer (White, angled in Studio):** a Heading 2, a Paragraph 2 of two or three
   sentences, and three numbered blocks.
3. **Proof (Navy):** a Heading 2 and three white cards with an image (square corners), a Heading 3
   and a short Paragraph 2 each. A Navy notch below it.
4. **Call to action (Warm White):** a Heading 2, one line of Paragraph 1, a primary button and a
   secondary button side by side.
5. **Footer (Black):** the white logo, links in Cyan and small print in Paragraph 3, in White.

## Part 4: Custom CSS (optional, Wix Studio)

**Skip this part unless you need it.** The settings above get you nearly all the way. CSS (the
code language that styles web pages) fixes two things Studio's settings cannot:

1. **Capital letters on headings, eyebrows and buttons.** Site Styles has no capitals setting, so
   without CSS you have to type them in capitals.
2. **One button style for the whole site.** Site Styles has no button styles, so without CSS you
   style every button by hand.

**Which editors.** Wix's developer documentation describes this CSS feature for Wix Studio. Some of
Wix's pages also mention the Wix Editor, but in practice the CSS option does not appear for most
Wix Editor sites. If you use the Wix Editor and do not see **global.css** in the steps below, skip
to Part 5, or simply keep typing headings in capitals and copying your saved buttons.

**Plans.** Wix's help pages list no plan requirement for CSS editing in Studio. Users in the Wix
Studio community report that it works on free plans too.

### Where to paste it

1. Click the **Code** icon on the left side of the editor. If it is your first time, click
   **Start Coding**.
2. Click **Page Code**.
3. Under **CSS**, click **+ Add global.css** (or click **global.css** if it is already there).
4. Paste the snippets below into `global.css`. CSS here applies to every page.

CSS in `global.css` overrides what you set in the Inspector, so after you paste it, change those
elements here rather than in the panels.

### Snippet 1: headings in capitals

This works with a custom class, a label you attach to one element so the CSS can find it.

1. Paste this into `global.css`:

   ```css
   /* Propellant website styles: see github.com/masschallenge/propellant-web */
   .propellant-headline,
   .propellant-headline .rich-text__text {
     text-transform: uppercase;
   }

   .propellant-eyebrow,
   .propellant-eyebrow .rich-text__text {
     text-transform: uppercase;
     letter-spacing: 0.3em;
   }
   ```

2. Select a heading text box. Keep the code panel open, and under **CSS Classes**, type
   `propellant-headline` in the **Custom classes** field. Give eyebrows `propellant-eyebrow`.
3. Now type the text in normal sentence case. It shows in capitals on the page, and screen readers
   read it as normal words.

### Snippet 2: every button as a Propellant pill

This uses `.button`, the class Wix gives every button, so it styles all of them at once.

```css
/* Propellant website styles: see github.com/masschallenge/propellant-web */
.button {
  border: 2px solid #00708e;
  border-radius: 999px;
  box-shadow: none;
  padding: 14px 28px;
  background-color: #00708e;
}

.button:hover {
  background-color: transparent;
}

.button__label {
  font-family: "Oswald", sans-serif;
  font-size: 16px;
  font-weight: 600;
  line-height: 1;
  letter-spacing: 0.05em;
  text-transform: uppercase;
  color: #ffffff;
}

.button:hover .button__label {
  color: #00708e;
}

.button.propellant-button-secondary {
  background-color: transparent;
}

.button.propellant-button-secondary:hover {
  background-color: #00708e;
}

.propellant-button-secondary .button__label {
  color: #00708e;
}

.propellant-button-secondary:hover .button__label {
  color: #ffffff;
}

.propellant-dark-section .button {
  background-color: transparent;
  border-color: #54eeff;
}

.propellant-dark-section .button:hover {
  background-color: #00708e;
  border-color: #00708e;
}

.propellant-dark-section .button__label,
.propellant-dark-section .button:hover .button__label {
  color: #ffffff;
}
```

Then add classes where you need the variations:

- **Secondary button:** select the button and type `propellant-button-secondary` under
  **Custom classes**.
- **Navy, Black or Deep Teal section:** select the section and type `propellant-dark-section`
  under **Custom classes**. Every button inside it turns into a Cyan outline that fills with Teal
  on hover. You still set the section's background and White text in the Inspector, as in Part 3.

The class names `.button`, `.button__label`, `.rich-text` and `.rich-text__text` come from Wix's own
documentation, which says only documented class names stay stable. Do not change them to other
names you find in the page.

### Check and remove

- Preview the site and check that buttons are pills in Oswald capitals and the headings are in
  capitals.
- **To remove the CSS later:** open **global.css** again, delete the snippet (from its comment line
  to its last `}`), and publish. Then remove the custom classes from the elements, or leave them:
  they do nothing without the CSS.

## Part 5: Custom code in the page head (optional, last step)

**Most sites do not need this.** It loads the Propellant stylesheet, the small file of ready-made
styles from the [website spec](/web/websites/#the-propellant-stylesheet). The head is a hidden part
of every page where browsers look for things like stylesheets.

**Requirements:** a published site with a connected domain, which needs a paid plan. Custom code
does not run on the free `wixsite.com` address, and you will only see its effect on the published
site, not in the editor.

**When it helps:** in Wix Studio, if you want to use the Propellant class names directly instead of
the snippets in Part 4. The stylesheet only styles elements you give one of its class names, using
the **Custom classes** field from Part 4, so it never changes the rest of your site. In the Wix
Editor there is usually no way to attach class names, so this step does little there.

1. Go to your site's dashboard and click **Settings**.
2. Under **Development & integrations**, click **Custom Code**.
3. Click **+ Add Custom Code** at the top right.
4. Paste this:

   ```html
   <!-- Propellant website styles: see github.com/masschallenge/propellant-web -->
   <link
     rel="stylesheet"
     href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/masschallenge/propellant-web@v2.0.0/dist/website.css"
   />
   ```

5. Name it `Propellant stylesheet`.
6. Under **Add Code to Pages**, choose **All pages**, and load it on each new page.
7. Under **Place Code in**, choose **Head**.
8. Click **Apply**, then publish the site.

The classes you can then use:

| Custom class | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `propellant-headline` | Heading 1 from the spec: the headline, in Oswald SemiBold capitals. |
| `propellant-eyebrow` | The tracked Oswald eyebrow above a headline. |
| `propellant-title-1`, `propellant-subhead`, `propellant-title-3` | Heading 2, Heading 3 and Heading 4 from the spec. |
| `propellant-body` | Paragraph from the spec. |
| `propellant-caption` | Paragraph small, in Slate, for dates and notes. |
| `propellant-text` | Body font and text color for a whole section. |
| `propellant-link` | An underlined link: Teal on light, Cyan on dark. |
| `propellant-section-navy`, `propellant-section-black`, `propellant-section-deep-teal` | A dark section with White text. |
| `propellant-section-warm-white`, `propellant-section-angled` | A light section, plain or with the angled tint. |
| `propellant-notch` | The notch below a section. |
| `propellant-card` | A white card with square corners. |

The stylesheet also loads Lato and Oswald for you. Wix adds a custom class to the outer edge of an
element, while Wix's own styling sits on the parts inside it (such as a button's label). If a
class does not seem to change something on the published site, use the Part 4 snippets instead,
which aim at Wix's own documented inner classes.

**To remove it later:** go back to **Settings**, **Custom Code**, find **Propellant stylesheet**,
open its menu and delete it, then publish.

## Check your work

On desktop:

- [ ] Headings, eyebrows and buttons are Oswald, in capitals. Paragraphs are Lato in Black
      `#222222`, in sentence case.
- [ ] Heading 1 is 64px, Heading 2 is 40px, paragraphs are 17px with a line height of 1.5.
- [ ] Primary buttons are Teal pills with White Oswald text, and clear to a Teal outline on hover.
- [ ] Secondary buttons are Teal outlines that fill with Teal on hover.
- [ ] Dark sections have White text, Cyan accents and Cyan outline buttons, and no Teal text.
- [ ] Dark and light sections alternate, with about 96px of space above and below and a notch where
      they meet.
- [ ] Images and cards have square corners.
- [ ] The logo is the official file, at least 24px tall, with clear space, linked to the home page.

On a phone (use the editor's mobile view, then check the published site on a real phone):

- [ ] Heading 1 is about 40px and paragraphs about 16px.
- [ ] Sections have about 64px of space above and below.
- [ ] Buttons are still pills and easy to tap.
- [ ] The site icon shows in the browser tab (paid plans only, and it can take a while).

## If something looks off

- **A text element ignores the theme.** It was styled by hand. Select it and choose the right style
  from the text style drop-down again (in the Wix Editor, **Edit Text**, then **Styles**). Text
  added from **Add Elements** under the themed options follows the theme by default.
- **A heading looks too heavy or too thin.** The wrong Oswald weight is selected. Pick **Oswald
  SemiBold** (weight 600), and make sure Bold is off for Headings 1 to 4.
- **Buttons are square or rounded only a little.** The corner value is too small. Set corners to
  `100` in the button's design settings, or add Snippet 2 in Studio.
- **The mobile site looks different from desktop.** The Wix Editor's mobile view and Studio's
  breakpoints can each have their own sizes and backgrounds. Switch to the mobile view and fix the
  element there.
- **The CSS or stylesheet does nothing.** In Studio, check that the class is typed exactly, with no
  dot and no spaces, in **Custom classes**. Head code only runs on the published site with a
  connected domain, so check there, not in the editor.
- **Colors look slightly off.** Retype the hex codes from the spec. Wix's base color shades are
  generated automatically, so pick the exact color you saved rather than a nearby shade.

# WordPress

Source: https://propellant.masschallenge.org/web/websites/wordpress/

This guide gives a WordPress site the MassChallenge look: Lato for text, Oswald headlines in
capitals, the brand palette, pill shaped Oswald buttons, dark and light sections and the logo in the
right places. Most of it is point and click.
Plan on about an hour the first time, and less if your theme is already close.

WordPress comes in a few shapes, and the steps depend on yours. Find your setup in the table, then
follow only the parts marked for it.

| Your setup | How to tell | Follow |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **A. Block theme** | Your dashboard has **Appearance > Editor**. Themes such as Twenty Twenty-Five work this way. | Setup A in every part |
| **B. Classic theme** | Your dashboard has **Appearance > Customize** but no **Editor**. | Setup B in every part |
| **C. Page builder** | You build pages with a plugin such as Elementor, and the plugin has its own site settings. | Setup C notes |

If you are starting a new site, pick a block theme (setup A). It gives you the most control without
code.

## Before you start

**Which WordPress you have matters for custom code.**

- **Self-hosted WordPress (WordPress.org):** every feature in this guide is free. You need to be an
  Administrator.
- **WordPress.com:** the style settings in Part 1 work on every plan. Custom CSS (Part 4) needs a
  paid plan: WordPress.com lists it for the Personal, Premium, Business and Commerce plans. Uploading
  a child theme or installing a plugin (the advanced route at the end of Part 4) also needs a paid
  plan. Plans change, so check your plan page if a menu is missing.

**Your WordPress version changes a few menu names.** We point these out as we go. You can see your
version at the bottom of any dashboard screen, or under **Dashboard > Updates**.

**Have these open:**

- The [website spec](/web/websites/) in another tab. Every value in this guide comes from it.
- The logo files, downloaded to your computer. Open each link and save the image:
  - [Horizontal logo, color](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/masschallenge/propellant-web@v2.0.0/assets/logos/masschallenge-logo-horizontal-color.png)
    for white and light backgrounds.
  - [Horizontal logo, white](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/masschallenge/propellant-web@v2.0.0/assets/logos/masschallenge-logo-horizontal-white.png)
    for Navy, Black, Deep Teal and other dark backgrounds.
  - [Monogram, color](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/masschallenge/propellant-web@v2.0.0/assets/logos/masschallenge-logo-monogram-color.png)
    for the site icon (the small picture in the browser tab).
  - The same folder also has `-black` versions, and a `masschallenge-logo-monogram-white.png`.

Upload the logo files to WordPress yourself, through the steps in Part 2. Do not link to a copy of
the logo from another website.

## Part 1: Set up site styles (no code)

This is the heart of the job. Set fonts, colors and buttons once here, and every page follows.

### Setup A: block themes (Site Editor and Styles)

In a block theme, **Styles** is one panel that controls the whole site: fonts, colors, spacing and
the default look of each type of block. WordPress calls these "global styles". Whatever you set
here applies everywhere, unless someone has styled a single block by hand.

#### Step 1: Open Styles

1. In the dashboard, go to **Appearance > Editor**.
2. Click **Styles** in the left menu, or the half filled circle icon at the top right.
3. If a welcome guide appears, close it.

You will move between three main sections: **Typography**, **Colors** and **Blocks**. The **Save**
button is at the top right. Save after each step so nothing is lost.

If your theme offers **Browse styles** (ready made style variations), you can ignore them. You are
about to set your own.

#### Step 2: Add Lato and Oswald with the Font Library

The Font Library installs fonts on your own site, so visitors do not load them from Google.

1. Open the Font Library:
   - **WordPress 7.0 or later:** go to **Appearance > Fonts** in the dashboard.
   - **WordPress 6.5 to 6.9:** in **Styles**, click **Typography**, then the **Manage fonts** button
     (an icon next to the **Fonts** heading).
   - **WordPress.com:** use whichever of the two your dashboard shows.
2. Click the **Install Fonts** tab. The first time, click **Allow access to Google Fonts**.
3. Search for **Lato**. Click it, tick **400 (Regular)** and **700 (Bold)**, also tick **400 Italic**
   if you use italics, then click **Install**.
4. Search for **Oswald**. Click it, tick **400 (Regular)**, **600 (SemiBold)** and **700 (Bold)**,
   then click **Install**.
5. Click the **Library** tab and check both fonts are listed.

If you would rather not connect to Google, download Lato and Oswald from Google Fonts on your
computer and add the files on the **Upload** tab instead (it accepts .ttf, .otf, .woff and .woff2).

#### Step 3: Create a font size for each text style

WordPress has no separate phone sizes. Instead it uses "fluid" sizes: you give a smallest and a
largest size, and the text scales smoothly between them as the screen gets wider. That is how you
get both the desktop and mobile sizes from the spec.

1. In **Styles**, click **Typography**, then **Font sizes** (in some versions this sits under a
   **Presets** heading).
2. Add a size for each row below. Click **+** (Add font size) to create one, or click an existing
   size to change it.
3. Give it the name from the table, turn on **Custom fluid values**, and enter the minimum and
   maximum.

| Name | Minimum (phones) | Maximum (desktop) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Heading 1 | 40px | 64px |
| Heading 2 | 30px | 40px |
| Heading 3 | 24px | 30px |
| Heading 4 | 20px | 24px |
| Eyebrow | 14px | 14px (turn **Custom fluid values** off and enter 14px) |
| Big stat | 48px | 72px |
| Paragraph large | 18px | 20px |
| Paragraph | 16px | 17px |
| Paragraph small | 14px | 14px (turn **Custom fluid values** off and enter 14px) |
| Button | 16px | 16px (turn **Custom fluid values** off and enter 16px) |

If you do not see **Custom fluid values**, your theme has fluid type switched off. Enter the desktop
size for each one, and add the "Phone sizes" snippet in Part 4.

#### Step 4: Set the typography for each element

An "element" is a kind of text WordPress styles across the whole site: text, links, headings,
captions and buttons.

1. In **Styles**, click **Typography**. Under **Elements**, click **Text** and set:

   | Setting | Value |
   | --- | --- |
   | Font | Lato |
   | Size | Paragraph |
   | Appearance (the weight) | Regular (400) |
   | Line height | 1.5 |
   | Letter spacing | 0 |
   | Letter case | None (no change) |

2. Go back and click **Headings**. Choose the **All** tab and set **Font** to Oswald, **Appearance**
   to SemiBold (600), **Letter spacing** to 0 and **Letter case** to Uppercase. Every heading level
   now starts from Oswald SemiBold capitals.
3. Set each heading level's size and line height on its own tab:

   | Tab | Size | Line height |
   | --- | --- | --- |
   | H1 (the headline) | Heading 1 | 1 |
   | H2 | Heading 2 | 1 |
   | H3 (subhead) | Heading 3 | 1.1 |
   | H4 | Heading 4 | 1.15 |

4. Go back and click **Captions**: Lato, size **Paragraph small**, Regular (400), line height 1.5.
5. Go back and click **Buttons**: Oswald, size **Button**, SemiBold (600), line height 1, letter
   spacing 0.05em (pick the **em** unit), letter case Uppercase.
6. Leave **Links** on the default, so links match the text around them.
7. Click **Save**.

Type headings and button labels in normal sentence case: the capitals come from the style, so the
words stay readable to screen readers and search engines. Paragraphs are never in capitals.

Paragraph large is for the odd standout paragraph, such as the line under a headline. Pick the
**Paragraph large** size on that paragraph when you write it.

#### Step 5: Add the color palette

The palette is the set of colors offered in every color picker on the site. You will add the spec
colors so nobody has to type a hex code again.

1. In **Styles**, click **Colors**, then **Palette**.
2. Under **Custom**, click **+** to add a color. Click the new color, type its name and enter the
   hex value. Repeat for every row:

   | Name | Hex | Use it for |
   | --- | --- | --- |
   | White | `#FFFFFF` | Light section background |
   | Warm White | `#F8F8F5` | Alternate light section background |
   | Light tint | `#F3FAFC` | The angled tint on a light section |
   | Navy | `#10263F` | Dark section background |
   | Black | `#222222` | Body text, and dark section background |
   | Deep Teal | `#004F73` | Dark section background |
   | Teal | `#00708E` | Headings, links and buttons on light |
   | Cyan | `#54EEFF` | Text, links and outlines on dark sections only |
   | MC Blue | `#0EABBC` | Graphic shapes only, never text |
   | Slate | `#4B575B` | Secondary text on light, such as captions |
   | Line | `#DBE1E3` | Lines and dividers |
   | Yellow | `#FFC801` | One warm accent: tags, rules and stats, with Black text |
   | Error | `#BF0261` | Form errors only |

3. Click **Done**.

The other warm accents (Orange, Raspberry and Lime) are for graphics, not for site text, so they
are not in the palette. Use one warm accent per page, in small doses.

Your theme also has its own **Theme** colors, and its header, footer and patterns use them. To keep
those parts on brand, open the three dots menu next to **Theme**, choose **Edit colors**, and
change each one to the closest spec color. Names vary by theme. If yours uses names such as Base,
Contrast and Accent, set **Base** to White `#FFFFFF` and **Contrast** to Black `#222222`, then look
at where each Accent appears on your site and give it the spec color for that job (for example, an
accent used for links becomes Teal `#00708E`, a light background accent becomes Warm White
`#F8F8F5`, and a dark background accent becomes Navy `#10263F`).

#### Step 6: Set the colors for each element

1. In **Styles > Colors**, under **Elements**, set:

   | Element | Setting | Color |
   | --- | --- | --- |
   | Background | | White `#FFFFFF` |
   | Text | | Black `#222222` |
   | Links | Default | Teal `#00708E` |
   | Headings | All | Teal `#00708E` |
   | Headings | H1 | Black `#222222` |
   | Captions | Text | Slate `#4B575B` |
   | Buttons | Text | White `#FFFFFF` |
   | Buttons | Background | Teal `#00708E` |

2. Click **Save**.

#### Step 7: Style the primary and secondary buttons

The Button block comes with two built in "block style variations": **Fill** and **Outline**. A block
style variation is a ready made look you can pick for a single block. Fill is the primary button
and Outline is the secondary button, so anyone editing a page can switch between them with one
click.

1. In **Styles**, click **Blocks**, then search for and click **Button**.
2. Set the default (Fill) look:
   - **Color:** Text White `#FFFFFF`, Background Teal `#00708E`.
   - **Typography:** Oswald, size Button, SemiBold (600), line height 1, letter spacing 0.05em,
     letter case Uppercase.
   - **Dimensions > Padding:** 14px top and bottom, 28px left and right. Click the link icon to set
     the sides separately.
   - **Border & Shadow:** border 2px, solid, Teal `#00708E`, no shadow, and **Radius** 9999px. A
     radius bigger than the button makes the ends fully round, which is the pill shape. Never use
     a smaller radius: square cornered buttons are retired.
3. If the panel shows a **Hover** state, choose it and set Background to none (transparent) and
   Text to Teal `#00708E`, so the fill clears to a Teal outline. Many versions do not offer hover
   for all buttons at once. In that case the button snippet in Part 4 adds it.
4. Find the style variations (shown as **Fill** and **Outline**, near the top of the Button panel)
   and click **Outline**. Set:
   - **Color:** Text Teal `#00708E`, Background none (transparent).
   - **Border:** 2px, solid, Teal `#00708E`. Keep the same radius, padding and typography as above.
   - **Hover**, if offered: Background Teal `#00708E`, Text White `#FFFFFF`.
5. Click **Save**.

The secondary button is still called "Outline" in the editor, which matches how it looks.

#### Step 8: Set the page width, images and sections

1. In **Styles**, click **Layout** and set **Content** width to 720px. This keeps paragraphs to
   about 68 characters a line. Leave **Wide** as it is.
2. In **Styles > Blocks**, click **Image**, open **Border & Shadow** and set **Radius** to 0. Photos
   and cards have square corners.
3. Click **Save**.

#### Step 9: Check on a phone

At the top of the Site Editor, open the **Preview** menu (a screen icon in some versions) and choose
**Mobile**. Check that the headline is smaller and still on one or two lines, and that buttons fit.
Switch back to **Desktop** when you are done.

### Setup B: classic themes (the Customizer)

Classic themes put their settings in the Customizer. Each theme builds its own Customizer, so the
panels differ from theme to theme. WordPress itself always gives you **Site Identity** and
**Additional CSS**. Fonts, colors and buttons depend on what your theme offers.

1. Go to **Appearance > Customize**.
2. Look for a **Colors** panel (it may be called **Colors & Dark Mode**, **Global** or **Design**).
   Match your theme's color slots to the spec:

   | Common theme label | Spec color |
   | --- | --- |
   | Background color | White `#FFFFFF` |
   | Text color, Body text | Black `#222222` |
   | Heading color | Teal `#00708E` |
   | Primary, Accent, Link color | Teal `#00708E` |
   | Link hover, Accent hover | Deep Teal `#004F73` |
   | Button background | Teal `#00708E` |
   | Button text | White `#FFFFFF` |
   | Button hover background | White `#FFFFFF`, with Teal text if the theme lets you set it |
   | Border, Divider | Line `#DBE1E3` |
   | Alternate background, Light background | Warm White `#F8F8F5` |
   | Dark background, Footer background | Navy `#10263F` |

   Turn off any dark mode switch, so the colors stay as set.

3. Look for a **Typography** or **Fonts** panel. If you find one, set body text to Lato, Regular
   (400), 17px, line height 1.5, and headings to Oswald, SemiBold (600), uppercase, letter spacing
   0. Then set H1 to 64px with line height 1, and use the H2 to H4 sizes and line heights from the
   spec. If your theme has separate mobile sizes, enter the sizes in brackets from the spec (H1
   40px, H2 30px, H3 24px, H4 20px, text 16px).
4. Look for a **Buttons** panel. If you find one, set the corner radius as high as it goes (or
   9999px), padding to 14px top and bottom and 28px left and right, a 2px Teal border, and font to
   Oswald SemiBold (600) at 16px, uppercase, letter spacing 0.05em.
5. Click **Publish**.

No Typography panel? That is common in classic themes. Use the "Classic theme fonts and text"
snippet in Part 4. On WordPress 7.0 or later you can also install Lato and Oswald in **Appearance >
Fonts** (Step 2 of setup A), but a classic theme still needs the snippet to use them.

Your pages and posts still use the block editor, so the Group, Cover and Buttons steps in Part 3
work for you too.

### Setup C: page builders such as Elementor

A page builder has its own global settings, and they win over the WordPress theme on the pages it
builds. Set them once and the builder's widgets follow. In Elementor:

1. Open any page with **Edit with Elementor**, click the Elementor menu at the top left, and choose
   **Site Settings**.
2. Under **Design System > Global Colors**, set the four system colors, then add the rest of the
   spec colors as custom colors with the same names and hex values as the palette table in Step 5
   above:

   | Elementor slot | Spec color |
   | --- | --- |
   | Primary (used by headings) | Teal `#00708E` |
   | Secondary | Navy `#10263F` |
   | Text | Black `#222222` |
   | Accent (used by buttons) | Teal `#00708E` |

3. Under **Design System > Global Fonts**, set:

   | Elementor slot | Font |
   | --- | --- |
   | Primary (headings) | Oswald, 600, uppercase, line height 1 |
   | Secondary (eyebrows) | Oswald, 400, 14px, uppercase, letter spacing 0.3em |
   | Text | Lato, 400, line height 1.5 |
   | Accent (buttons) | Oswald, 600, 16px, uppercase, letter spacing 0.05em |

   Add one more global font named **Big stat**: Oswald, 700, line height 1. Pick it on large
   numbers only.

4. Under **Theme Style**, set **Typography** for body text and H1 to H4 with the sizes from the
   spec (Elementor lets you switch to tablet and mobile sizes with the device icon next to each
   size). Set **Buttons** to Teal `#00708E` background, White text and a 2px Teal border, with a
   transparent background and Teal text on hover, a large border radius for pill ends, and 14px by
   28px padding.
5. Click **Update**.

Other page builders have the same ideas under different names, usually "global colors", "global
fonts" and "theme style". Use the same mapping.

## Part 2: Add the logo and site icon

The site icon is the small picture in the browser tab and on phone home screens. WordPress needs it
square, at least 512 by 512 pixels. The monogram file is wider than it is tall, so first place it in
the middle of a square, at least 512 by 512 pixel canvas, in any image editor. Leave space around
it and never stretch it. Save that as a PNG.

### Setup A: block themes

1. Go to **Appearance > Editor** and click **Identity** in the left menu (newer versions). Click the
   **Site Logo** area and upload `masschallenge-logo-horizontal-color.png`. Click the **Site Icon**
   area and upload your square monogram.
2. No **Identity** menu? Open **Patterns > Template Parts > Header** (in older versions,
   **Template Parts > Header**), click the **Site Logo** block and upload the logo there. Set the
   site icon in **Settings > General > Site Icon** (WordPress 6.5 or later) or in the Site Logo
   block's settings.
3. Select the Site Logo block in your header and set its **Image width** to about 240px. That shows
   the logo about 32px tall. Never go below 180px wide (24px tall): the brand minimum is 160px wide,
   and below 24px tall the name is hard to read, so use the monogram instead.
4. In the block's settings, turn on **Link image to home** if your theme offers it.
5. Click **Save**.

If your header has a Navy, Black or Deep Teal background, use
`masschallenge-logo-horizontal-white.png` there. The color logo is only for White and Warm White
backgrounds.
